items.title: Hasan Nawaz's fighting 96 against India in vain as Pakistan settle for Asian Games cricket silver
items.description: Hasan Nawaz’s fighting 96 went in vain as Pakistan fell 19 runs short of India’s 212-run target to settle for silver in the Asian Games men’s cricket final at the Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin, Japan on Saturday. Hasan struck five fours and seven sixes in his 51-ball innings before being caught behind off Shivam Dube from the final ball of the match, with Pakistan finishing on 192 for six. Needing 33 from the last over after reaching 179 for five, Pakistan kept their hopes alive when Hasan hit Dube for a boundary and then a six. But a yorker from the India all-rounder followed by two dot balls left Hasan needing four for his century from the final delivery. He attempted to clear the infield but was caught by wicket-keeper Sanju Samson, ending an innings that had briefly brought Pakistan back into contention. Hasan’s dismissal completed a remarkable recovery after Pakistan had been 39 for three after six overs. He and Saim Ayub put on 87 for the fourth wicket before Saim was dismissed for 29 off 22 balls in the 15th over. Hasan had reached his half-century from 28 balls and continued to attack India’s spinners, particularly Ravi Bishnoi, who conceded 44 from his three overs. Pakistan’s Saim Ayub (L) makes it to the crease to avoid a runout during the men’s cricket final match between Pakistan and India during the 2026 Asian Games at the Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin on October 3, 2026. Pakistan were 126 for three after 14 overs, requiring 86 from the last 36 balls, but Dube removed Saim and Abdul Samad in successive stages of the closing overs to keep India ahead. Saim was caught by Washington Sundar at square leg for 29 after attempting to use Dube’s pace, while Samad made nine before being caught by Tilak Varma off Washington in the 18th over. Despite those setbacks, Hasan continued the assault. He reached 68 from 36 balls after hitting Axar Patel for a six in the 16th over and then struck two fours in Dube’s next over, one of them coming through an edge after he flashed at a short, wide delivery. Pakistan reached 160 for four after 17 overs, needing 52 from the final 18 balls. India’s players celebrate the dismissal of Pakistan’s Abdul Samad during the men’s cricket final match between Pakistan and India during the 2026 Asian Games at the Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin on October 3, 2026. — AFP Saad Masood kept the chase alive with two sixes in his unbeaten 12 off five balls, but Bumrah’s fourth over yielded only 11 runs, leaving Pakistan 33 short with six balls remaining. Dube was given the final over and conceded a boundary and a six to Hasan, but his yorkers at the crucial moment denied Pakistan the chance to complete the chase. India’s bowlers had earlier kept Pakistan under pressure after the batters had posted 211 for six. Pakistan’s chase had begun brightly enough but lost momentum after Sahibzada Farhan and Usman Khan departed in successive overs. Farhan made 10 off 11 balls before attempting a slog-sweep against Sundar and finding Patel at deep midwicket. Usman followed for three off six, slogging a fuller delivery from Patel to Dube at midwicket. Maaz Sadaqat, who made 23 off 18 balls with three fours, was then caught by Sundar off Patel at the start of the seventh over to leave Pakistan 39 for three. Hasan and Saim rebuilt the innings, taking Pakistan to 76 for three at the halfway stage. Hasan was then 26 off 18 and Ayub 12 off nine. The pair accelerated through the middle overs, with Hasan reaching his half-century from 28 balls. Their 87-run partnership gave Pakistan a realistic chance of chasing India’s imposing total, but Dube’s dismissal of Saim at 126 proved a significant turning point. Varma stars India had earlier been propelled to 211 for six by Varma and Dube, who added 62 from 31 balls for the sixth wicket. Varma remained unbeaten on 51 off 22 balls, striking three fours and four sixes, while Dube made 27 off 15 with two fours and two sixes. India had lost three wickets between the eighth and 15th overs after making an explosive start, but the late partnership lifted them beyond 200. Abhishek Sharma provided the initial impetus with 61 off 28 balls, hitting three fours and seven sixes. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made 15 off nine before being caught by Usman off Saim, while Sanju Samson was dismissed for two by Ahmed Daniyal. Shreyas Iyer made 21 off 24 balls and Ishan Kishan 20 off 18. Ishan fell to Arafat Minhas at 128, while Iyer was dismissed by Abrar Ahmed five runs later. India reached 114 in the first 10 overs before adding 97 in the second half of the innings. Varma reached his half-century from 21 balls and remained unbeaten, while Dube was dismissed by Daniyal in the first ball of the final over. For Pakistan, Arafat took two for 25 from three overs and Daniyal two for 43. Abrar took one for 29 and Saim one for 47. Saad and Sufyan Moqim went wicketless. Sri Lanka took the bronze medal after beating Bangladesh by 63 runs in the third-place playoff.

items.title: Man found shot dead in UK van transporting migrants in France
items.description: A man has been found shot dead in a UK tradesman’s van carrying irregular migrants parked in a rest stop along a northern French motorway, officials said Saturday. The vehicle was found on Friday, around 30 kilometres (20 miles) north of the city of Troyes, which is located southeast of Paris and around 300 kilometres from the Channel, according to the local prosecutor’s office. A suspect “believed to have been present at the crime scene” was arrested early Friday, Troyes’s prosecutor Isabelle Verissimo said. The body of the 47-year-old man was discovered around 5:00 am (0300 GMT) with “a gunshot wound to his head” on a seat inside the van, which had UK licence plates, she said. Inside the vehicle police found “around 10 foreign nationals who were irregularly on French territory”, she added, without giving their nationalities nor that of the deceased man. An initial investigation suggested shots were fired in the Champ l’Epée rest stop as the UK van stopped to park there, and several people then fled the scene, according to the prosecutor’s statement. The law enforcement office in Reims, north of where the crime happened, was in charge of the investigation. The Troyes prosecutor’s office said a criminal case would be opened on Saturday for “murder, attempted murder, unauthorised possession of a weapon, aiding the irregular entry, the movement and the residence of a foreigner in France as part of an organised group, and human trafficking as part of an organised group”. items.title: La Russie appelle les diplomates et étrangers à quitter Kiev, ciblée à répétition
items.description: La Russie a appelé une nouvelle fois samedi les diplomates et étrangers se trouvant à Kiev à quitter la ville, avertissant que ses forces continueront de mener des « frappes de représailles massives » contre la capitale ukrainienne, ciblée à répétition depuis des semaines. Un nouveau grand pont y a été frappé samedi matin après une journée de vendredi marquée par de gigantesques embouteillages dans une bonne partie de la ville, créés par plusieurs attaques de drones russes sur une autre structure permettant de traverser le Dniepr. Réitérant un premier appel de ce type formulé en mai, le ministère russe des Affaires étrangères a suggéré dans un communiqué aux « ressortissants étrangers et aux diplomates se trouvant à Kiev à quitter la ville ». « La responsabilité des éventuelles conséquences négatives incombe entièrement à ceux qui ignorent cet avertissement », a-t-il averti, annonçant que « les forces armées russes continueront de mener des frappes de représailles massives » contre « des cibles militaires à Kiev et dans d'autres villes ukrainiennes ». Le précédent avertissement de Moscou il y a plusieurs mois n'avait pas été suivi par les chancelleries occidentales qui soutiennent l'Ukraine et une cinquantaine d'États avaient qualifié à l'ONU ces messages de « menaces » contre les diplomates présents à Kiev. La capitale ukrainienne a été particulièrement prise pour cible ces dernières semaines par des vagues quasi-quotidiennes de drones, et notamment de drones à réaction plus difficiles à intercepter, au moment où l'Ukraine fait face à un manque de moyens antiaériens. – Chaos routier – Samedi matin, le pont Nord, l'une des huit structures qui enjambent le fleuve Dniepr, a été touché par des bombardements russes, a annoncé sur Telegram le maire de la capitale Vitaly Klitschko. La surface de la route et les câbles des trolleybus ont été endommagés sur le pont, qui a été coupé à la circulation dans le sens rive gauche-rive droite du fleuve, a-t-il affirmé. Jeudi et vendredi, c'est le pont Sud qui avait été touché à plusieurs reprises par des drones russes, entraînant sa fermeture à la circulation et un chaos routier dans la métropole de trois millions d'habitants. Il s'agissait des premières attaques importantes contre un pont majeur de Kiev depuis le début de l'invasion russe en 2022. Depuis longtemps, l'Ukraine redoutait de telles frappes. M. Klitschko a qualifié vendredi la situation dans la capitale d' »extrêmement dramatique » et estimé que Moscou était en train de « saccager » la ville en s'en prenant systématiquement à ses infrastructures et sa logistique. L'Ukraine et la Russie ont nettement fait monter en puissance leurs frappes à longue portée ces derniers mois, faisant un nombre croissant de victimes civiles. Pour Kiev, particulièrement ciblée, cela se traduit par des sirènes d'alerte aérienne retentissant sans cesse. Moscou a aussi dévasté le secteur de la métallurgie de l'Ukraine et mis à l'arrêt une bonne partie de ses exportations agricoles en mer Noire, portant un coup à son économie. Des stations-services, centres commerciaux, centres de données informatiques et opérateurs téléphoniques ont aussi été pris pour cibles. En Russie, ce sont les raffineries et dépôts de pétrole qui sont visés, ce qui avait provoqué une crise du carburant cet été, ou encore les entrepôts des géants du e-commerce Wildberries et Ozon. – Arrivée de l'hiver – Après avoir lancé cet été une opération infructueuse de « 40 jours » pour faire chavirer l'économie russe, le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky multiplie depuis les propositions de trêve dans les frappes. Une telle idée a été rejetée par son homologue Vladimir Poutine jeudi. « On nous dit : +Qu'ils cessent de frapper vos raffineries, et vous cesserez de frapper leurs navires+. C'est tout simplement ridicule », a lancé le président russe lors du forum politique de Valdaï. L'Ukraine craint surtout l'arrivée de l'hiver, période critique lors de laquelle ses infrastructures énergétiques peuvent être prises pour cible. Lors de l'hiver 2025, la Russie avait dévasté les centrales ukrainiennes, plongeant par moments des millions de personnes dans le froid et dans le noir, par des températures glaciales. « Les Ukrainiens sont conscients que cet hiver pourrait être très rude pour nous. Mais face à cela, nous n'aurons d'autre choix que de le rendre pénible pour la Russie également », avait déclaré M. Zelensky à la tribune de l'ONU fin septembre. AFP L’article La Russie appelle les diplomates et étrangers à quitter Kiev, ciblée à répétition est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Boat carrying over 70 mourners capsizes in Benue, several missing
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A wooden boat conveying more than 70 mourners and over 30 motorcycles across the River Katsina-Ala at the Buruku Local Government Area, LGA, crossing point in Benue State, capsized Saturday morning, leaving several passengers missing. The incident occurred at about 11am as the passengers, said to be mostly from Mbayon in Gboko LGA, were returning from the burial of a relative on the other side of the river. Several passengers were reportedly rescued following the mishap, while search and rescue operations continued as of Saturday afternoon for those still unaccounted for. An eyewitness in the area said the boat was heavily overloaded when its engine reportedly developed a fault midway into the journey. According to the eyewitness, “The boat was overloaded with many people and over 30 motorcycles, and they were coming from the Logo LGA side of the River at about 11am when the incident happened. “Many persons have been rescued, but as we speak, I cannot tell you the actual number of persons that have not been seen or rescued from the river because the search is still ongoing. But many persons have not been seen as we speak.” Confirming the incident, the Chairman of Buruku Local Government Area, Mr Raymond Zege, said the victims were mourners from Gboko who had crossed the river to attend a burial. Zege said the boat had more than 70 persons on board when its engine failed during the return journey, creating panic among the passengers. According to him, “The victims were mourners from Gboko who went for a burial on the other side of the river. They boarded a boat which was overloaded with over 70 persons. In the middle of the journey the engine of the boat failed, and they became panicky. “And they also ran into a heavy wave, and the boat capsized before the boat that was sent to rescue them got to them.” The council chairman said the exact number of missing passengers had yet to be established, adding that rescue workers had already recovered a large number of the passengers. “At the time we speak, we do not know the number of persons missing. So far we have not seen about six persons, but we have rescued over 60. Search and rescue operations are ongoing,” he said. Zege also appealed to residents and other commuters using the waterway to comply with maritime safety regulations, particularly the use of life jackets. He said the local government had provided life jackets for commuters using the route but noted that some passengers often resisted efforts by maritime workers to enforce their use. “People can be very difficult. There is a law, and we have provided life jackets for every commuter crossing that route. When they come and the maritime workers try to enforce the law, some commuters complain that they have health issues or that they do not want to share life jackets used by other people. “We have provided the jackets, and the state government is also supporting efforts to ensure that maritime safety regulations are enforced,” he said. According to the chairman, “Sometimes the maritime officials come for enforcement, including at night. People should cooperate with them because the safety measures are meant to protect lives,” he said. Meanwhile, the Benue State Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, Hon. Denis Iyaghigba, confirmed the incident in a statement he personally signed on Saturday. The commissioner said he had received preliminary reports of the mishap and urged families and members of the public to remain calm while authorities continued efforts to establish the number of persons involved and rescue those who might still be trapped or missing. “I have received preliminary reports of an unfortunate boat mishap at the Buruku crossing point this morning, Saturday, 3rd October, 2026,” Iyaghigba said. “I wish to assure members of the public, particularly families of those who may have been aboard the boat, to remain calm and await verified information from the appropriate authorities. No effort will be spared to ensure their safety.” Iyaghigba said he had directed boat operators and their union downstream to mobilise and support the ongoing search and rescue operation. “I have directed the boat operators and their union downstream to mobilise and assist in the ongoing search and rescue operation,” he said. He added that “further details will be communicated as the rescue operation progresses.” As of the time of filing this report, search and rescue operations were still ongoing, while authorities had yet to release a final figure for the number of passengers aboard the boat and those still missing. items.title: Kintinian : un double éboulement fait deux morts dans l’orpaillage clandestin à Köfilani
items.description: Dans la nuit du 1er au 2 octobre 2026, un double éboulement survenu à Bouré Köfilani, dans la préfecture de Kintinian, a coûté la vie à deux (2) jeunes orpailleurs. Ce drame relance le débat persistant sur la dangerosité de l’orpaillage clandestin, pratiqué au mépris des interdictions en cette période de fortes pluies. Malgré la suspension officielle décrétée par les autorités et la surveillance exercée sur le terrain par les chasseurs traditionnels (donzos), des chercheurs d’or clandestins continuent de s’immiscer furtivement sur les sites miniers. C’est au cours de l’une de ces incursions nocturnes, rendues particulièrement périlleuses par l’état détrempé des sols en cette saison des pluies, que la tragédie a frappé. Le premier éboulement a coûté la vie à un premier orpailleur. Son corps a été rapidement évacué par ses compagnons d’infortune, et ce, à l’insu des autorités locales de Köfilani. En raison de cette évacuation précipitée et clandestine, l’identité civile de cette première victime n’a pas pu être établie avec précision par notre équipe de reportage. Le deuxième éboulement a nécessité des recherches plus ardues pour retrouver les proches. La victime a finalement été formellement identifiée : il s’agit de Mamadjouma Mara, âgé de 25 ans, fils de Sadou et de Yamasadjö, marié à une (1) femme et père de zéro enfant. Il résidait à Boukaria, au quartier Foufalati, et était originaire du village de Gnarya, dans la préfecture de Dinguiraye. Le corps de Mamadjouma Bah a été enterré ce vendredi soir, aux environs de 18 heures, au grand cimetière de Boukaria, dans le recueillement et la tristesse de ses proches et de sa famille. Interrogé sur ce énième accident mortel, le secrétaire administratif du bureau de district de Köfilani a exprimé sa désolation face à l’obstination de certains orpailleurs : « ça fait longtemps que l'orpaillage artisanal a été suspendu sur notre terre mais les orpailleurs resistants tentent toujours. C'est ce qui est dangereux avec les fortes pluies en ce moment. » Il a, par ailleurs, adressé une mise en garde stricte à l’encontre des récalcitrants, prévenant qu’ils s’exposent désormais à de vives poursuites judiciaires et devront répondre de leurs actes devant la loi. Ce double accident de Bouré Köfilani rappelle, de la manière la plus tragique, que la terre ne pardonne pas l’imprudence, surtout lorsque la nature est fragilisée par les intempéries. Au-delà de la stricte interdiction administrative, c’est une question de survie et de protection de la vie humaine qui est engagée. La recrudescence de ces pratiques clandestines exige aujourd’hui une réponse concertée, associant la fermeté judiciaire des autorités, la vigilance accrue des comités de veille locaux et une prise de conscience collective des dangers mortels encourus dans les fosses aurifères clandestines. Mamoudou Kéïta, correspondant à Kintinian 628 61 88 90 L’article Kintinian : un double éboulement fait deux morts dans l’orpaillage clandestin à Köfilani est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Zio/Assainissement : 44 latrines remises aux populations des cantons de Gape-Kpodzi et Gape-Centre
items.description: Tsévié, 3 oct. (ATOP) – Quarante-quatre latrines familiales réalisées grâce à l’appui de l’Association Dzidzo dans les cantons de Gapé-Kpodzi et Gapé-Centre dans la commune Zio 4 ont été officiellement remises aux bénéficiaires, le vendredi 2 octobre à Gapé-Kpodzi. Les latrines sont réalisées dans quatre villages des deux cantons à savoir : Gapé-Kpodzi, Agokopé et Agokopé Kpédomé dans le canton de Gapé-Kpodzi et à Aloyi dans le canton de Gapé-Centre. Ces installations sanitaires sont réalisées dans le cadre de la phase 3 du projet « Mettre fin à la défécation à l’air libre » de l’Association à travers l’approche Assainissement total piloté par les communautés (ATPC). Ce projet a bénéficié de l’accompagnement des services techniques de la direction préfectorale de la santé du Zio. L’objectif est d’améliorer l’accès des populations de Gapé-Kpodzi et Gapé-Centre à des installations sanitaires adéquates, de promouvoir l’hygiène et l’assainissement dans les communautés et de réduire les risques de maladies liées à la défécation à l’air libre. Il s’agit aussi de préserver la salubrité et l’environnement, d’améliorer les conditions de vie et le bien-être des populations. Pour la réalisation de ces latrines, l’Association Dzidzo a appuyé les bénéficiaires en ciment et sollicité l’expertise technique de la direction préfectorale du Zio. Le reste a été assuré par les bénéficiaires eux-mêmes. C’est des latrines ventilées à double fausses amovibles qui servent à produire de l’engrais biologique pour les cultures. Le représentant du directeur préfectoral de la Santé du Zio, Batchassido Essohana Karbou a relevé les dangers liés à la défécation à l’air libre. Il a mentionné, à titre d’exemple, la propagation des maladies diarrhéiques, notamment la diarrhée, la dysenterie et le choléra. De plus, il a cité la contamination de l’eau et des aliments par les matières fécales, la transmission de parasites intestinaux, le risque de fièvre typhoïde et de poliomyélite. M. Batchassido a, par ailleurs, rappelé aux bénéficiaires les bonnes manières à adopter pour mieux entretenir et gérer ces latrines durablement. Pour le secrétaire général de l’Association Dzidzo, Batao Kossi Mawunya, la réalisation de ces latrines constitue une étape importante dans l’amélioration des conditions d’hygiène et de la santé des populations. Il a invité tous les bénéficiaires à en faire un usage effectif et approprié, à veiller à leur entretien et à sensibiliser leur entourage sur les dangers liés à la défécation à l’air libre. « Mettre fin à la défécation à l’air libre est une responsabilité collective pour une communauté plus saine, plus propre et plus digne » a conseillé le représentant du maire de la commune Zio 4, M. Amouzou Kofi. Les représentants des bénéficiaires des quatre villages concernés ont fait des témoignages sur l’importance de disposer des latrines familiales. Ils n’ont pas manqué de témoigner leur reconnaissance à l’Association Dzidzo pour l’aboutissement de ce projet. ATOP/BBG/SED/KYA

Kintinian en fête : clôture magistrale de la Semaine de l’indépendance dans la nouvelle préfecture
items.description: La nouvelle préfecture de Kintinian, rattachée à la nouvelle région administrative de Siguiri, a vibré au rythme de la fête de l’indépendance, ce 2 octobre 2026. Lancées officiellement depuis le 25 septembre sous le sceau de la « semaine de l’indépendance », conformément au programme officiel consolidé par la ministre de l’Administration du territoire et de la Décentralisation, Mme Camara Djènèbou Touré, les festivités du 68e anniversaire de l’accession de notre pays à la souveraineté nationale se sont déroulées dans une ambiance de joie manifeste et sans le moindre incident. L’événement a été rehaussé par la présence de M. Souleymane Sidibé, directeur national adjoint du MATD, venu spécialement assurer la supervision de ces festivités historiques pour la localité. La journée s’est articulée autour des grands moments solennels prévus par le comité d’organisation : La montée des couleurs nationales, un instant d’intense ferveur patriotique partagé par toute l’assistance ; La pose de la gerbe de fleurs, un vibrant hommage rendu aux pionniers de la liberté guinéenne ; Une liesse populaire, marquée par une communion parfaite entre les autorités civiles, militaires et les citoyens de Bouré-Kintinian, dans une atmosphère festive. Porte-parole de toute la communauté de Bouré, le doyen d’âge, Elhadj Siaka Camara, et sa suite ont formulé de fervents vœux de réussite et de paix pour le pays : « Bonne fête au président de la république et à sa Famille, à Madame la ministre, au gouvernement, ainsi qu'à l'ensemble des citoyens. Que Dieu benisse la Guinée ! ». Pour couronner cette semaine de célébrations, un grand dîner a été organisé à la résidence du nouveau préfet, le capitaine de police Mohamed Lamine Koïta. Ce banquet de clôture a réuni, dans un esprit de cohésion totale, les autorités administratives et communales, les chefs locaux, ainsi que les groupements de femmes, scellant ainsi la fin d’une commémoration historique, parfaitement réussie à Kintinian. Mamoudou Kéïta, correspondant à Kintinian 628 61 88 90 L’article Kintinian en fête : clôture magistrale de la Semaine de l’indépendance dans la nouvelle préfecture est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Burkina : 153 Messagers formés pour propager les valeurs de la Révolution progressiste populaire
items.description: Le Cabinet africain pour le développement et l’efficacité professionnelle, en collaboration avec la Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso, a organisé, ce samedi 3 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou, la cérémonie officielle de remise du Manifestes de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP) à 153 Messagers . Cette cérémonie de clôture, marquant la fin de trois jours de formation, a été présidée par le Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo. Ils sont total 153 Burkinabè, issus de toutes les couches socioprofessionnels à avoir reçu ce samedi, leurs manifestes de la Révolution progressiste populaire. Selon le coordonnateur du programme, Bienvenue Hounkponou, l’initiative est née de la volonté de porter le message de la Révolution aux quatre coins du Burkina Faso, afin de permettre aux populations de mieux s’approprier ses valeurs, sa vision et son concept. Une vue des officiels « Le message de la Révolution progressiste populaire, sa compréhension au fond, doit être accessible à toutes les filles et à tous les fils du Burkina Faso » , a-t-il déclaré. Le Premier ministre remettant le manifeste à une messagère Cette première promotion regroupe 153 messagers issus de divers milieux socioprofessionnels, notamment des étudiants, des serviteurs du peuple, des députés à l’Assemblée législative, des hommes de lettres et des artistes. Ils sont 153 citoyens Burkinabè à avoir été formés aux valeurs de la Révolution Cette diversité de profils vise, selon le Coordonnateur, à permettre au programme de toucher les différentes couches sociales du pays. L’initiative est également appelée à évoluer et à s’élargir à d’autres messagers. Plus de détails à suivre sur Minute.bf .

Treat healthcare as an investment, not a budget cost – Mahama
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has called on African governments and investors to fundamentally change the way they approach healthcare financing, arguing that health must be treated as an investable economic sector rather than a social expenditure to be funded only when resources are available. Addressing the Health Plenary of the Alamein Africa Forum in Alamein, Egypt, on Saturday, October 3, President Mahama said investment in health was central to Africa’s economic transformation, human capital development, job creation and macroeconomic stability. He said the continent could no longer afford to regard healthcare simply as a cost on national budgets. “For decades, African Finance Ministers and global investors have made a fundamental error: they have treated health as a line-item cost—a social expenditure to be funded only when there is budget left over,” President Mahama said. “Health is not a charitable cause; it is an investable, high-growth economic sector.” He cited evidence of the economic returns from healthcare investment, including findings that targeted basic emergency maternal and newborn care could generate significant economic and social returns for every dollar invested. He also referenced research by the Lancet Commission indicating that reductions in mortality accounted for nearly a quarter of total income growth in developing economies in the early 2000s. President Mahama said a stronger health sector would not only improve the wellbeing of citizens but also strengthen national economies. “Investing in health strengthens our balance sheets rather than depleting resources,” he said, urging governments, private capital, commercial banks, industrial developers and sovereign funds to view health investment as an important component of Africa’s economic future.

items.title: NY governor vows to close loophole after alleged Cornell gang rape
items.description: New York Governor Kathy Hochul vowed Friday to close a legal loophole that makes it harder to prosecute rape cases if the victims were willingly intoxicated, amid an uproar over an alleged gang rape at Cornell University. The accuser in that case has filed a civil lawsuit over the alleged 2024 attack at the Ivy League school, casting a harsh spotlight on a decision by prosecutors not to file any criminal charges at the time. The investigation into the incident was reopened on Monday, and Hochul has appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor, as anger mounts over allegations that Cornell failed to properly hold the men accountable. In her civil suit, the woman says she was drugged with ketamine, assaulted and raped by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity, a social club for male students. “It should not matter whether they chose to use drugs or alcohol. Voluntary intoxication is not a license for sexual assault or gang rape. Period,” Hochul said Friday. “I support closing this loophole, and will work with the New York state legislature to accomplish this.” Several US states, including New York, have provisions in their laws making it harder for prosecutors to bring charges against someone who engaged in sex with a person who voluntarily became intoxicated to the point where they could not meaningfully give — or withhold — consent. “It’s just astounding that this loophole still exists,” Shiwali Patel, the senior director of education justice at the National Women’s Law Center, told AFP. “It does have a huge impact on college cases because the reality is that a significant majority of campus sexual assaults do involve alcohol and drugs.” In the United States, one in four female undergraduates reported forced sexual contact or sexual contact for which they could not consent, according to a 2020 study of 33 institutions by the Association of American Universities. – ‘Deeply disturbed’ – Hochul slammed how the initial investigation into the complainant’s claims unfolded at Cornell, which is located in Ithaca in central New York state. “She sat for hours and told (police) exactly what happened to her. And according to new reports, she could not have been clearer that she was 100 percent confident that she had been raped,” Hochul said. “In what world would the police learn from a victim that she’d been literally gang-raped while intoxicated… in the fraternity house, and not elevate those allegations to the district attorney?” James, a Democrat who has clashed repeatedly with US President Donald Trump, said Friday she would “review the facts, gather evidence, interview witnesses, and if warranted, pursue prosecutions.” Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said this week that he planned to file criminal charges against the seven men. He said his office declined to prosecute in 2024 because the complainant’s testimony did not establish a lack of consent. Following the allegations, Cornell shut down the fraternity and temporarily suspended the students allegedly involved, several of whom were later expelled. Lawyer Thomas Giuffra, who represents the alleged victim, told CBS News that his client was “incapable of consent” because she was “completely, grossly intoxicated” when she arrived at the frat house. “I’m more and more convinced there was a cover-up” to protect the university’s reputation, Giuffra added. Cornell’s student body held a campus meeting Thursday at which emotions ran high. Speakers repeatedly attacked college administrators for their handling of the case, which has garnered nationwide attention. “No public official gets to look the other way when the system breaks down and fails our young people. And as governor, I will not allow anyone to sweep this case under the rug,” Hochul said Friday. “I am deeply disturbed by Cornell University’s police and how they handled this.” In Washington, Trump lashed out at James’s involvement as special prosecutor, saying: “I feel badly for whoever she’s looking at, because they won’t get a fair shake.” The post NY governor vows to close loophole after alleged Cornell gang rape appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Droits humains : le ministère de la Justice instaure un dialogue annuel avec la société civile
items.description: Le ministre de la Justice, Garde des Sceaux, Me Moussa Sarr, a institué une journée annuelle de dialogue avec les organisations de la société civile engagées dans la promotion et la protection des droits humains. Fixée au 21 octobre de chaque année, cette rencontre vise à instaurer un cadre permanent d’échanges sur les droits humains et la bonne gouvernance, avec un mécanisme de suivi des recommandations formulées. Un cadre permanent de concertation À travers l’arrêté n°031180 du 1er octobre 2026, le ministère de la Justice met en place une journée de dialogue annuel entre le Garde des Sceaux et les organisations de la société civile actives dans la promotion et la protection des droits humains. Placée sous l’autorité et la direction du ministre de la Justice, cette initiative vise à créer une plateforme durable de concertation entre le département ministériel et les acteurs de la société civile. Les échanges porteront notamment sur les questions relatives aux droits humains et à la bonne gouvernance. Le texte s’inscrit dans le cadre des missions du Conseil consultatif national des droits de l’Homme et du droit international humanitaire, dont le ministre de la Justice assure la présidence. Il se réfère notamment au décret n°2018-1969 du 15 novembre 2018 fixant les missions, la composition et le fonctionnement de cette instance. Des contributions attendues des organisations L’arrêté fixe au 21 octobre de chaque année la tenue de cette journée, en référence à la Journée africaine des droits de l’Homme. Les organisations de la société civile souhaitant participer aux échanges devront transmettre, au plus tard le 7 octobre de chaque année, un mémorandum de 30 pages au maximum. Ce document devra présenter leurs préoccupations et leurs recommandations sur les questions liées aux droits humains et à la bonne gouvernance. Les contributions devront être déposées au secrétariat du cabinet du ministre de la Justice ou à la Direction des droits humains. Chaque organisation participante devra également désigner un à trois porte-parole. Ces représentants seront chargés de présenter le mémorandum lors de la rencontre et de coordonner les interventions des autres membres de la société civile. Un mécanisme de suivi des recommandations Au-delà des échanges annuels, le dispositif prévoit un mécanisme de suivi des recommandations formulées lors des rencontres précédentes. Ainsi, au début des travaux de chaque édition, le ministre de la Justice présentera un rapport sur la mise en œuvre des recommandations issues de la journée de dialogue de l’année précédente. Ce rapport sera élaboré par le secrétaire permanent du Conseil consultatif national des droits de l’Homme et du droit international humanitaire, sur la base des contributions des points focaux et des informations communiquées par la société civile et les autres acteurs concernés. Cette disposition vise à assurer une continuité entre les différentes éditions de la rencontre et à permettre aux participants d’apprécier les suites réservées à leurs propositions. Un financement assuré par le budget du Conseil L’organisation de cette journée annuelle sera financée par le budget du Conseil consultatif national des droits de l’Homme et du droit international humanitaire. Avec ce dispositif, le ministère de la Justice formalise un cadre de dialogue régulier avec les organisations de la société civile. La périodicité de la rencontre, les modalités de contribution des participants et l’obligation de présenter un rapport de suivi constituent les principaux mécanismes prévus par l’arrêté pour structurer cette concertation autour des droits humains et de la bonne gouvernance. C.G.D

items.title: Mahama outlines Ghana’s strategy to expand healthcare and produce medicines locally
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has outlined Ghana’s strategy to expand healthcare access while developing the country’s capacity to produce medicines, vaccines and other health products locally. Addressing the Health Plenary of the Alamein Africa Forum in Egypt, President Mahama said Ghana was implementing what he described as the “Accra Reset” through a combination of expanded healthcare coverage and measures designed to strengthen domestic health-sector production. He said the agenda included the expansion of the National Health Insurance Scheme, the introduction of Free Primary Health Care and the establishment of the Ghana Medical Trust Fund. “In Ghana, we are implementing the Accra Reset by expanding the National Health Insurance Scheme, introducing Free Primary Health Care, establishing the Ghana Medical Trust Fund,” President Mahama said. He added that the government was also empowering the Food and Drugs Authority and the National Vaccine Institute as part of efforts to move Ghana from a consumer to a producer of health products. The President said the strategy was intended to position Ghana to participate more meaningfully in regional health value chains rather than relying heavily on imported health products. He argued that stronger domestic production could help retain foreign exchange, support industrial development and provide greater resilience against international supply disruptions. President Mahama said Ghana’s experience formed part of a broader continental effort to build a self-sustaining African health ecosystem. He pointed to Egypt’s experience in tackling Hepatitis C and Nigeria’s African Medical Centre of Excellence in Abuja as examples of African initiatives aimed at building domestic capacity and retaining health-related skills and resources on the continent. “We do not need to look outside our continent for proof that this works,” he said.

items.title: Okpebholo threatens to arrest contractor over abandoned Benin-Abraka road
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu Governor of Edo State, Monday Okpebholo, has threatened to arrest the contractor handling a section of the Benin-Abraka Road for allegedly abandoning the project after receiving payment from the previous administration. The road connects Edo and Delta state from that axis. The governor made this threat while speaking to members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Orhionmwon and Uhunmwode local government areas during his ongoing tour to strengthen the party ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement on Saturday by his Chief Press Secretary, Dr. Patrick Ebojele, the governor said he had taken a decision to address the condition of the road but was constrained by contractual agreements entered into by the previous administration. He said the road was awarded to two contractors, with one of them currently making progress on its section, which he said was about 75 per cent complete. According to him, “Following the agreement that was signed by Obaseki’s administration, that road construction project was paid for before I became governor. Despite the payment by the previous administration, the contractor still abandoned the road, allowing motorists to suffer untold hardship passing through the road. “That road was given to two contractors. One of them is working and is doing his job and has gotten up to 75 per cent completion, while the other, who is a friend to Obaseki, has abandoned his section and has become the problem causing hardship on the road.” The governor said he had previously avoided commenting publicly on the project but was compelled to address the matter after hearing complaints during his visit. “Those in the diaspora don’t know what is happening and for me as the governor, I never wanted to speak on the issue of this Benin-Abraka Road, but what I heard today has prompted me to speak on the issue. I am going to arrest that contractor,” he said. Okpebholo was accompanied by APC leaders and senior government officials during the visit, which also took him to Iguomo-Nisi in Uhunmwode Local Government Area, where he interacted with party members and mobilised support for APC candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. The Edo APC Chairman, Jarrett Tenebe, commended party members for turning out in large numbers to support the governor and the party. Tenebe also thanked voters for their support during the last local government elections and urged them to continue supporting the governor. items.title: Don’t pay attention to those who will distract you; Ghanaians are already disappointed – LPG tells NPP
items.description: The Liberal Party of Ghana (LPG) has urged the New Patriotic Party (NPP) to remain focused and united, cautioning them against individuals it says could distract the party from its political objectives. Delivering a solidarity message at the NPP’s National Delegates Conference in Kumasi on Saturday, October 3, the LPG said the conference presented an opportunity for the NPP to strengthen its democratic processes and unite its members. The party encouraged NPP members, including those who may be dissatisfied with developments within the party, not to allow internal disagreements to undermine the party’s unity. “Ghanaians are telling NPP that this is not the time to be listening to some baleful people that was within your political party that enjoyed positions.” The LPG further cautioned NPP members against individuals it said could seek to distract the party during the period of internal reorganisation. “Don’t pay attention to those who are going to distract you because Ghanaians are already disappointed.” The party also claimed that many Ghanaians were dissatisfied with the current state of affairs and said there was public interest in the return of NPP flagbearer and former Vice President, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia. “Ghanaians have already given up. Ghanaians are crying. And Mr. flagbearer, the former vice president, Ghanaians say they miss you and they want you, yourself, and your leadership.” The LPG said its message was not intended merely as praise for the NPP’s flagbearer but as what it described as an observation of the political mood in the country. “I’m not here just to sing praises, but I’m just trying to be factual.” The party also used its solidarity message to emphasise the importance of democratic processes and political tolerance. “Let us encourage democracy because what we are experiencing now as government is saying something else. People being harassed, the intolerance attitude.” The LPG said it was pleased to see political parties engage in democratic processes and encouraged NPP members to maintain unity as the party elects its national officers. The NPP is holding its National Delegates Conference at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi, with more than 7,000 delegates expected to participate in the election of national officers. The conference also includes consideration of proposed amendments to the party’s constitution.

items.title: Prof Mike Oquaye praises NPP Minority’s performance in Parliament
items.description: Former Speaker of Parliament, Prof Mike Oquaye, has praised the performance of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) Minority Caucus in Parliament, saying the group has made a strong impact despite having fewer members than the governing majority. Prof Oquaye said the Minority had performed particularly well in holding the government to account and described its limited numbers as unfortunate. Speaking to JoyNews on the sidelines of the NPP Delegates Conference in Kumasi, he was asked whether he was impressed with the performance of the current Minority Caucus. “Oh, I think the caucus is doing very, very well,” Prof Oquaye said. “It is most unfortunate that they are small in number, but they are big in performance.” Prof Oquaye also spoke about the importance of the NPP electing national executives capable of working effectively with the party’s flagbearer, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, as the party prepares for the 2028 general election. He said delegates should look beyond popularity and consider the experience, track record and ability of candidates to work with others. “I expect leaders who have vision. They have a good track record,” he said. Prof Oquaye said the party would be watching the performance of the various candidates over time and would also consider their ability to work as a team. “Because we will be watching the performances of all these people over the years,” he said. “Not only that, but their capacity to cooperate with others. Particularly with the candidate and his team. That harmony is imperative.” According to Prof Oquaye, cooperation between the party’s national executives and its presidential candidate will be critical to the NPP’s chances in 2028. He warned that a lack of harmony could create divisions within the party and undermine its electoral prospects. “Otherwise, it creates internal party schisms which are not the best for victory,” he said. He said if the right leadership qualities were brought together and the party worked as a united force, there would be grounds for confidence ahead of the next election. “When these elements converge and come to play, we are confident about the future election,” he said. When asked whether his confidence in the NPP’s future extended to the 2028 presidential election and whether he believed Dr Bawumia could defeat the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Prof Oquaye expressed confidence in the NPP’s flagbearer. “That is so. We’ve got an excellent candidate. His track record is clear and manifest,” Prof Oquaye said. However, he said that the candidate alone would not be enough to secure victory, arguing that the NPP would need an effective party organisation to support him. “Nevertheless, we need a good party machine to support him to a sweet victory,” he said.

items.title: KAAF University vice chancellor urges fresh students to embrace technology, innovation
items.description: The Vice Chancellor of KAAF University, Professor Alhassan Musah, has urged newly admitted students to embrace technology and innovation to prepare themselves for the rapidly changing world of work. He says the world of yesterday is not the same as the world of today, and students must therefore acquire relevant skills and remain adaptable to succeed beyond the university. Professor Musah made the call at the university’s matriculation ceremony for about 1,750 newly admitted students. The newly admitted students have officially begun their academic journey at KAAF University, with the Vice Chancellor urging them to look beyond traditional academic qualifications. Professor Alhassan Musah encouraged the students to take advantage of technology and innovation to develop practical skills, create opportunities and prepare for emerging careers. He noted that technological advancement continues to transform industries and the nature of employment, making it necessary for young people to constantly update their skills. Professor Musah urged the students to use their time at the university to think creatively, develop practical competencies and position themselves to contribute meaningfully to national development. “This year’s matriculation is particularly significant, as we welcome 1,750 new students into the KAAF University community. Of this number, 745 are males, representing 42.6%, whereas 1,005 are females, representing 57.4%. As a university, we are committed to preparing graduates who can contribute meaningfully to national and global development. I therefore challenge you to cultivate an entrepreneurial mindset. Do not only ask, where can I find a job? Also ask, what problem can I solve? What value can I create?” The Vice Chancellor also cautioned the fresh students against indiscipline, urging them to make responsible conduct a key part of their university life. He asked them to respect the rules and regulations of the institution, manage their time effectively and develop habits that will support both their academic and personal growth. Professor Musah stressed that academic qualifications must go hand in hand with good character and responsible conduct. He reminded the students that discipline would remain important not only during their university education but also in their future careers. “Character is as important as competence. KAAF University expects you to conduct yourself with honesty, respect, discipline, responsibility, and integrity. Academic dishonesty, examination malpractice, plagiarism, racism, falsification of records, violence, and other forms of misconduct have no place in this great institution. “Your reputation begins with the choices you make today. Be punctual, keep your word, respect others, and take responsibility for your own actions. Remember that a successful graduate is measured not only by what he or she knows, but also by how that knowledge is used and the kind of person the graduate becomes.”

items.title: Bilawal says Centre was ready to impose emergency in KP but PPP sought 'political solution'
items.description: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Saturday said the federal government had made up its mind to impose emergency or governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; however, his party suggested finding a political solution to fight terrorism in a “better way”. Addressing an event in Karachi, Bilawal said that the federal government had been in contact with President Asif Ali Zardari and the PPP regarding the recent security situation, particularly in KP. Noting the terrorist attacks emanating from Afghanistan, Bilawal said, “In my opinion, the federal government had made up its mind and was 100 per cent ready; they wanted to immediately impose emergency or governor’s rule in KP.” He noted that although imposing governor’s rule or emergency in any province was a Constitutional tool, the PPP “was of the view that before dropping this constitutional atomic bomb, political parties should absolutely find a political solution to fight terrorism in a better way”. Sharing his party’s view, Bilawal said the PPP wanted to hold talks with the protesting party — the PTI — regarding its planned Oct 4 long march to Islamabad before making any decision. While calling on all parties to engage in dialogue with PTI before imposing emergency, he also urged the latter to abandon its long march to Islamabad and acknowledge the success of their protest. Bilawal said the PTI protest had been somewhat successful as the capital “has been shut for 10 days”, even if the party had not marched towards it. “A political party or worker should see that you have achieved success on the political stage.” However, he pointed out: “But it is also correct that while you are focusing on your own politics, there is terrorist activity in KP every other day. “If the provincial government does not consider this issue of terrorism and law and order important, and there are allegations that they are not standing with the federation, then we may be forced to declare an emergency or governor’s rule.” The PPP chief noted that the terrorist threat from Afghanistan and India’s “hideous role” in supporting it was apparent. “Do not see terrorism through a political lens.” “We want to come together to fight terrorism and not view it as a political issue, but a national one,” Bilawal emphasised, recalling a recent meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Zardari. The Bhutto scion called for a written agreement between the KP and federal governments which would outline “how they will combat terrorism together”. “If there is any political deadlock, it needs to be kept separate from issues like terrorism or national interests.” The government and PPP are jointly engaged in talks with the opposition, aimed at defusing the country’s ongoing political crisis. The discussions precede the PTI’s planned Oct 4 protest march demanding the release of party founder Imran Khan, which has emerged as the latest point of contention between the party and the federal government. The decision to have talks with the opposition was taken after PM Shehbaz called on President Zardari at Aiwan-i-Sadr in Islamabad earlier this week. National security, institutional cooperation on law and order and the possibility of using emergency powers were among the topics discussed. A joint delegation comprising PML-N and PPP leaders met the opposition on Friday, with a second round of talks held on Saturday. As the politicians gathered at Parliament House, National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq expressed hope that the talks would proceed in the same “cordial atmosphere” as the day before. Bilawal announces water projects for Karachi’s SITE Earlier in his speech, Bilawal congratulated the people of Karachi on the completion of a water project and added that the PPP saw its first success in local government elections. “We have started a 35m gallon water treatment project, and this water will fulfil the needs of SITE,” he stated. “The dirty water that used to pollute Karachi, our sea and our river will be treated, bringing benefits for all. In the second phase, 65 million gallons will be treated by January. Once this is completed, the capacity will reach 100 million gallons.” “The number one priority for us is water. Eight per cent of Sindh’s water comes through Irsa ,” Bilawal said, referring to the Indus River System Authority, which releases water downstream into Sindh. However, persistent water shortages due to Irsa not releasing sufficient water have triggered strong protests in the past. He said Karachi and Sindh “do not get our deserved share” as the 1991 Water Apportionment Accord has not been implemented. “Rather than giving us water, they pursue projects without our permission, which causes water shortages in Sindh and Karachi. “The Sindh government and KMC (Karachi Metropolitan Corporation) prioritised saving water for the people of Karachi, so that they can avail extra water,” Bilawal outlined, adding that several months ago, a 25m gallon water treatment facility was inaugurated in Kemari. “As the mayor told you, the capacity will be increased by 55 million gallons, so that we can deliver those benefits to the people of Kemari,” he added. Calling it the first project of its kind in Pakistan, Bilawal expressed hope that the needs of people in Karachi’s SITE area would be met, noting that it is the “engine” for the economy of the city and Pakistan. Additionally, the PPP chief noted that by Oct 20, projects to provide 10m gallons of water to Lyari and the Defence Housing Authority (DHA) through a pipeline would be completed.

items.title: Move beyond packaging to produce drug ingredients in Africa – Mahama to pharma industry
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has challenged African pharmaceutical companies and industrial investors to move beyond basic packaging and fill-and-finish operations towards the production of active pharmaceutical ingredients on the continent. Addressing the Health Plenary of the Alamein Africa Forum in Egypt, President Mahama said Africa’s ambition to achieve health sovereignty would remain incomplete if the continent continued to depend on external markets for the critical ingredients required to manufacture medicines. He said African governments, industrialists and investors needed to develop strategic partnerships capable of building deeper manufacturing capabilities, including research, biotechnology, pharmaceutical engineering and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) synthesis. “ What strategic partnerships do we need to move from basic packaging and fill-and-finish operations to full Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) synthesis on African soil?” he asked. The President said deeper local production would strengthen the continent’s resilience to international supply disruptions while creating opportunities for industrialisation and high-value employment. He argued that Africa’s large and growing population, combined with increasing demand for medicines and chronic disease treatment, provided a substantial market for investors willing to develop manufacturing capacity. President Mahama therefore urged industrial leaders, commercial banks, institutional investors and sovereign funds to participate in building a stronger African pharmaceutical ecosystem. He said governments must work alongside private capital to provide the financing, infrastructure and regulatory environment needed to support large-scale production. “Let us build factories, integrate supply chains, fund innovators, and secure our citizens’ future,” he said.

items.title: Lahore magistrate sends female suspect to jail on judicial remand in Azeri woman's rape case
items.description: LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Saturday sent a woman suspect to jail on a 14-day judicial remand in connection with a case of an Azeri woman’s rape. The 20-year-old Azerbaijan national had travelled to Pakistan for business purposes and was allegedly gang-raped by three men in a rented flat of a private housing society near Raiwind on the night between Sept 25 and Sept 26. Two of those men had been arrested and were sent on a six-day physical remand on Tuesday. In her statement , the complainant had named two women with whom she had met before the men accused of raping her gathered with them at an apartment. One woman had secured pre-arrest bail while the other was arrested and sent on a three-day physical remand on Wednesday. On Saturday, upon the completion of her remand, the police produced the woman suspect before Magistrate Azhar Mahmood. The investigating officer told the magistrate that as further custody of the suspect was not required for investigation, she could be sent to jail on judicial remand. Subsequently, the magistrate allowed the request and sent the suspect on a 14-day judicial remand until Oct 17. Meanwhile, Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Investigation Syed Zeeshan Raza noted that a total of three suspects have been arrested so far, while one was still at large. Addressing a press conference, the DIG said swabs of the survivor and the suspects were taken and sent to the forensic science agency for further investigation. The ages of the suspects were between 25 and 30 years. He also claimed that the suspects had confessed to their crime and police were continuing their investigation. DIG Raza said the suspects had threatened the woman for having contacts with influential people and stopped her from approaching the police. Survivor’s statement The Defence C police had registered a first information report (FIR) against three unidentified suspects on September 26 on the Azeri woman’s complaint. In her statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) , the survivor said she had arrived in Islamabad from Istanbul on Sept 13 and stayed in Faisalabad for five days before travelling to Lahore. “I had a plan to visit Skardu, but I could not go there because I was alone,” she said. According to her, on the day of the alleged incident, she messaged two women, asking them to meet her in Lahore. At around 11pm, she went to a cafe where she met one of them — the woman sent on remand today — and later accompanied her to a house in Bahria Town to meet the other, who has secured pre-arrest bail until Oct 5 . The complainant told the magistrate that at around 2am, a white car arrived carrying two men, one of whom was sent on remand on Tuesday (first suspect). Later, they moved to an apartment where two more men arrived, one of whom was the second person sent on remand (second suspect), while she did not know the name of the other man. According to the complainant, in a separate room, the woman on bail took between Rs20,000 and Rs30,000 from the first suspect, saying the money was for a party, while the woman now on remand also joined them. The Azeri woman said she made it clear that she “did not need money or alcohol”. She alleged that the first suspect tried to touch her and locked her in a separate room. When she asked about her friends, she was told that they had left. When she tried to leave, the complainant said she was told that she could not go because her friends had taken money. The victim said she offered to pay the men, but they told her that she would have to drink alcohol with them before they would let her go. She alleged that the three men raped her. She further stated that the suspects then put her in a car and threw her out at an unknown location, while threatening her with dire consequences if she approached the police. According to her statement, the suspects also took her handbag containing Rs200,000, an iPhone 13 Pro Max and another mobile phone. She then requested some people present there to help her call the police emergency number 15, following which the police arrived. It is the second such case in which a foreign woman was reportedly gang-raped in the Defence C police station area during the last four months. In June, two foreign women, nationals of the Netherlands and Venezuela, were allegedly abducted and sexually assaulted in the Defence C police station area. According to the FIR, the women were abducted by five suspects, including a close relative of a senior political personality, who demanded ransom and subjected them to sexual assault during their captivity.

items.title: Manhyia South MP Baffour Awuah pleads not guilty to EOCO charges, granted GH¢10m bail
items.description: Manhyia South Member of Parliament Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah has been granted GH¢10 million bail with two sureties after pleading not guilty to three charges brought against him by the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO). The bail was granted after prosecutors, led by Deputy Attorney-General Justice Srem-Sai, presented the charges against the legislator before the court. The two sureties are the Member of Parliament for Bosome Freho and the Member of Parliament for Effia. Baffour Awuah pleaded not guilty to charges including conspiracy to commit a crime and dissipation of public funds, as well as intentionally causing financial loss to the state. He also denied a money laundering charge relating to an alleged GH¢1 million transfer to the then Managing Director of SIC Life in 2024. The prosecution team includes Senior State Attorney Nana Ama Prempeh and EOCO officers Leo Anthony Asiamah, Emmanuel Dzakata and Rabiatu Abdulai, who are expected to assist with the state’s case. The charges form part of an EOCO investigation into alleged financial transactions involving SIC Life Savings and Loans. Baffour Awuah’s lawyer, Samuel Atta Akyea, has previously rejected the allegations and maintained that his client’s involvement in the matter arose from legitimate legal work undertaken for SIC Life. The latest proceedings follow the MP’s surrender to EOCO on October 1 after an Accra High Court issued a warrant for his arrest. EOCO subsequently confirmed that Baffour Awuah had surrendered and was cooperating with investigators. The case will now proceed through the court process, with the prosecution expected to present evidence in support of the charges.

items.title: NPP conference: We need leaders to complement our efforts in Parliament – Annoh-Dompreh
items.description: The Minority Chief Whip and Member of Parliament for Nsawam-Adoagyiri, Frank Annoh Dompreh, says the incoming national leadership of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) must work closely with the Minority Caucus to strengthen the party’s efforts in Parliament. He said the caucus was determined to play its role in Parliament and would need the support of the party’s national leadership to complement its efforts. Speaking ahead of the NPP’s National Delegates Conference in Kumasi on Saturday, October 3, Mr Annoh-Dompreh said the party needed leaders who would be prepared to take on national issues and provide effective opposition. “Well, we need leaders that would complement our effort. We are determined in parliament to constitute government and therefore we can’t do it all alone at that hand. We need the national leaders to come work with us then we can have a full complement and then join forces with our flagbearer.” He said a strong working relationship between the parliamentary caucus, the new national leadership and the party’s flagbearer would be necessary to advance the NPP’s political objectives. “Then we can blaze the necessary trails and resort the necessary avenues.” Mr Annoh-Dompreh also said the new leadership must be prepared to scrutinise the government and hold it accountable for its promises and deliverables to Ghanaians. He argued that the government was now experiencing the scrutiny that comes with being in office, after previously serving as an opposition party. “Now you can see that the government has really tasted how it feels like to govern. I mean when they were in opposition they said all sorts of things and now they are really coming under the scrutiny of the Ghanaian people.” He said he expected the incoming national executives to be determined and prepared to tackle national issues. “And so we are expecting a crop of leaders who would have a war-like thinking and don’t misquote me. I’m not saying we are going to take arms.” Mr Annoh-Dompreh explained that by “war-like thinking”, he meant a determination to confront national challenges and intensify the party’s oversight of government. “Determined to do battle, determined to tackle national issues, determined to take the fight to the government and also to properly execute oversight in terms of the deliverables that the government is supposed to deliver to the people.” On the conference itself, the Minority Chief Whip said the programme would involve two main processes, including the consideration of proposed constitutional amendments followed by the election of national officers. He expressed confidence that the process would be orderly and urged that the proceedings start and end as scheduled. “We expect a very smooth process and I’m very confident as you can see So far it’s been orderly typical of the New Patriotic Party.” He added: “I expect a very smooth process and I’m hoping that we can start on time and be able to finish as planned.” The NPP is holding its National Delegates Conference in Kumasi, where delegates are expected to consider proposed amendments to the party’s constitution before electing new national officers. The conference is part of the party’s internal reorganisation ahead of the 2028 general election.

items.title: Exposition gouvernementale: Le MATM dévoile ses acquis sous la RPP
items.description: Dans le cadre de la deuxième phase de la 3e édition des Journées d’Engagement patriotique et de Participation citoyenne (JEPPC), le ministère de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité (MATM) participe à l’exposition gouvernementale, du 2 au 9 octobre 2026 au Pavillon du Soleil Levant du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO). A travers son stand, le MATM présente au public ses principales réalisations, ses équipements, ses innovations et ses projets structurants enregistrés au cours des quatre années de la Révolution populaire progressiste (RPP). Conçu comme une vitrine des différents domaines d’intervention du ministère de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité (MATM), l’espace d’exposition met en lumière plusieurs secteurs, notamment l’administration territoriale, la mobilité, la protection civile, la météorologie et l’aviation civile. Des équipements emblématiques sont exposés à l’intérieur comme à l’extérieur du pavillon. Les visiteurs peuvent ainsi découvrir un bus de la Société de Transport en commun (SOTRACO), une ambulance blindée, une échelle aérienne, des mannequins équipés pour la protection contre les risques nucléaires, radiologiques, biologiques et chimiques (NRBC), des tenues de feu de la Brigade nationale de Sapeurs-Pompiers (BNSP), ainsi qu’un parc météorologique de l’Agence nationale de la météorologie (ANAM). Au-delà des équipements, le stand permet également aux visiteurs de mieux connaître les missions, les services et les innovations portés par les différentes structures placées sous la tutelle du MATM, notamment à travers la présentation du recueil des lois et décrets couvrant la période de septembre 2022 à septembre 2026, ainsi que du magazine trimestriel du ministère. L’exposition donne également une place importante aux structures techniques rattachées au ministère. Dans le domaine du transport aérien, Air Burkina présente notamment les maquettes de deux aéronefs de type Embraer 190, ainsi que ses services et produits. La Société des Aéroports du Faso (SAFA) expose, pour sa part, des maquettes de plusieurs projets structurants, dont la nouvelle aérogare de Bobo-Dioulasso, l’hôtel Silure et l’aérogare de Dori. Elle présente également son service de billetterie et l’Initiative « Génération SAFA ». Dans le domaine de la régulation et de la sécurité de l’aviation civile, l’Agence nationale de l’Aviation civile (ANAC) présente ses solutions numériques dédiées à la gestion des incidents d’aviation et à la digitalisation des badges d’accès aux aéroports. De son côté, la SOTRACO met en avant ses services et accompagne les visiteurs dans la découverte et l’utilisation de sa plateforme d’abonnement en ligne, contribuant ainsi à rapprocher davantage le transport public des usagers. L’Agence nationale de la Météorologie (ANAM) propose quant à elle, une immersion dans l’observation et le suivi des phénomènes météorologiques. Les visiteurs peuvent notamment découvrir l’évolution des phénomènes suivis en temps réel et mieux comprendre les services liés à l’information météorologique. Cette exposition gouvernementale constitue ainsi un cadre de proximité entre les services publics et les citoyens. Elle permet au MATM de donner à voir, de manière concrète, les équipements acquis, les solutions développées et les actions engagées dans ses différents domaines d’intervention. Du 2 au 9 octobre 2026, le ministère invite les populations à venir découvrir son espace, échanger avec les équipes mobilisées et mieux connaître les services proposés au public. DCRP/MATM L’article Exposition gouvernementale: Le MATM dévoile ses acquis sous la RPP est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Sammy Crabbe steps down from NPP Chairmanship race, backs John Boadu
items.description: Aspirant for the National Chairmanship of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Sammy Crabbe, has withdrawn from the race and endorsed fellow contender and former General Secretary, John Boadu. The announcement was made by Mr Boadu on social media ahead of the party’s National Delegates Conference in Kumasi on Saturday, October 3. Mr Boadu said Mr Crabbe had decided to step down from the contest and throw his support behind his candidature. “Sammy Crabbe, an aspiring National Chairman of the NPP, has stepped down from the race and thrown his support behind John Boadu. Let’s win together!” Mr Crabbe, a former Greater Accra Regional Chairman of the NPP, was one of four candidates who had been cleared to contest the National Chairmanship position alongside Mr Boadu, former National Chairman Paul Afoko and former Energy Minister Boakye Agyarko. The withdrawal means Mr Crabbe will no longer participate in the chairmanship election, which is taking place at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium as part of the NPP’s National Delegates Conference. Mr Boadu had earlier secured the first position on the ballot paper for the chairmanship contest, while Mr Crabbe picked the second position during the party’s balloting exercise in September. The NPP is electing its national officers as part of efforts to reorganise the party ahead of the 2028 general election, with more than 7,000 delegates expected to participate in the exercise.

items.title: NPP postpones constitutional amendments, including proposal on party leadership to next national conference
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has postponed consideration of proposed amendments to its constitution until its next national conference, citing time constraints at its ongoing National Delegates Conference in Kumasi. The decision was announced on Saturday, October 3, as the party prepared to proceed with the election of its new national executives. The proposed amendments were initially scheduled to be considered ahead of the national officers’ elections. However, the party said the limited time available would make it difficult for delegates to properly consider the proposals while also conducting the elections. The amendments will therefore be deferred to a subsequent conference to allow delegates adequate time to consider and deliberate on them. The proposals are expected to be fewer than 20 and include issues that were not addressed during the party’s previous constitutional amendment conference in Accra in January 2026, as well as new proposals that the party believes require further review. One of the key proposals concerns who should be designated as the leader of the NPP. The party had introduced a clause at its January 31 conference stating that the National Chairman would be the leader of the party at all material times. However, the latest proposed amendment seeks to revisit that arrangement and designate the party’s flagbearer as its leader. Other proposed changes include reforms to the structure of the national vice-chairmanship and communications and information technology positions. The decision to defer the amendments means the current conference will focus on the election of the party’s new national executives. A total of 7,163 delegates are expected to participate in the conference and national officers’ elections at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi. The Electoral Commission is supervising the elections, which form part of the NPP’s reorganisation ahead of the 2028 general election.

items.title: Formation du gouvernement : le RNI confirme sa volonté de participer
items.description: Le Conseil national du Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI), réuni ce samedi à l’occasion de sa session extraordinaire, a confirmé la disposition du parti de la « Colombe » à participer au prochain gouvernement, en mandatant son président pour gérer cette participation conformément à ce que commande l’intérêt national, selon un communiqué du parti. Le communiqué ajoute que « le Conseil national a exprimé sa grande fierté à l’égard du bilan positif réalisé par les ministres et parlementaires du parti durant la dernière législature, ainsi que de l’ampleur des réformes structurelles qui ont contribué à consacrer un Maroc de la dignité, de l’égalité et de l’égalité des chances ». Il a également salué « l’esprit de responsabilité qui a marqué l’action du gouvernement dirigé par Aziz Akhannouch, ainsi que les efforts nationaux qu’il a déployés pour assurer la cohésion des composantes de la majorité et garantir l’efficacité de son action en matière de gestion et sur le plan institutionnel ». Le communiqué a par ailleurs salué « le climat positif dans lequel se sont déroulées les dernières élections législatives », y voyant « une confirmation du choix démocratique sous la conduite de Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu l’assiste, depuis son accession au trône de ses glorieux ancêtres ». Il souligne que « les résultats obtenus par le parti lors des dernières élections, malgré le recul enregistré, constituent une expression claire et concrète du fait que le Rassemblement national des indépendants demeure une véritable force politique, disposant de tous les atouts nécessaires pour résister, assurer sa continuité et tirer les enseignements de cette expérience », notamment après cinq années de gestion gouvernementale et compte tenu de leurs conséquences et de leur coût politique. Les membres du Conseil national du parti ont félicité la direction et les militants du Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM) à l’occasion de son arrivée en tête des dernières élections législatives. Ils ont également félicité Fatima Zahra Mansouri pour « la haute confiance royale dont elle a bénéficié à l’occasion de sa nomination à la tête du gouvernement, dans le plein respect du choix démocratique et des dispositions constitutionnelles », exprimant leur fierté de la place accordée par le Souverain à la femme marocaine. Le communiqué précise également que « le président Mohamed Chouki a présenté devant les membres du Conseil national du parti le rapport politique », dans lequel il a abordé les principales évolutions de la scène politique, économique et sociale du pays, ainsi que les différentes questions liées à l’organisation interne du parti. Il a également exposé les positions du parti sur les questions internationales actuelles et les défis régionaux, à la lumière des constantes du Royaume et de ses intérêts supérieurs. Ce rapport a souligné que « les chantiers de réforme et les projets structurels mis en œuvre durant le mandat gouvernemental dirigé par Aziz Akhannouch ont traduit une forte volonté politique de faire face aux défis, de renforcer la résilience de l’économie nationale, de contribuer à l’amélioration de la position du Royaume dans les indicateurs de développement humain et de consolider les fondements de l’État social ». Le Rassemblement national des indépendants a enfin renouvelé « sa profonde fierté à l’égard de la diplomatie sage menée par Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu l’assiste, pour défendre l’intégrité territoriale du Royaume ». Le parti a salué les reconnaissances internationales successives concernant la question du Sahara marocain, dans la perspective d’un règlement définitif de ce qu’il qualifie de « conflit artificiel », ainsi que la consécration de l’initiative d’autonomie comme solution définitive et réaliste, dans le cadre de la souveraineté du Royaume et de son intégrité territoriale.
