items.title: We got funds for constituency projects during emergency rule – Rivers lawmaker
items.description: By Davies Iheamnachor, PORT HARCOURT The lawmaker representing Emohua State Constituency at the Rivers State House of Assembly, Hon. (Mrs) Justina Emeji, has revealed that the lawmakers got funding to execute projects during the period of emergency rule declared in the state by President Bola Tinubu. Emeji, who is the deputy chief whip of the 10th Assembly, made this disclosure during the inauguration of one of her constituency projects, Echonwere Royal Hall in Okporowo Ogbakiri Clan in the Emohua Local Government Area of the state. Emeji in her address commended President Bola Tinubu and the Minister of Federal Capital Territory, Chief Nyesom Wike, for their efforts in ensuring the development of the state. Emeji said, “I want to thank President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. It was during the emergency rule this money was released to us. “When we got the money, our speaker (Martin Amaewhule) asked me to go and put something on the ground so that my people would remember me. That was how I came home to do this.” She disclosed that aside from the commissioned town hall, she had seven other people-orientated constituency projects going on across the 14 wards of the LGA. She said the projects, which included a lodge for corps members at Oduoha Ogbakiri, a market at Isiodu Emohua, six classroom blocks at Ibaa Community, teachers’ quarters at Akpabu, six classroom blocks at Egbeda and another six classroom blocks at Ovogo Community, would impact positively on the people. Emeji further empowered 150 persons from the 14 wards of the LGA with N30m as an empowerment fund. However, the Speaker of the State House of Assembly, Hon. Martin Amaewhule, hailed Emeji for being a dependable member of the 10th Assembly, adding that she has not failed her people. He said, “We are here to commission one of the projects nominated by Hon. Justina Emeji for her constituency, which is this town hall right behind me. She nominated these projects after consulting with her people, and they said they want these projects. “She ensured that the project is supervised and completed, and today this town hall is ready for use,” Amaewhule said. Amaewhule stressed that representation is a core mandate of a legislator, involving identifying the needs and aspirations of constituents and working with government to actualise them. He noted that before the 2027 general election, the state would witness a harvest of constituency projects across all constituencies. He said, “Let me also re-emphasise that she has seven other projects that are ongoing. That shows that she is representing her people well. The 10th Rivers State House of Assembly has members that are representing our people effectively and delivering on their mandates.” The post We got funds for constituency projects during emergency rule – Rivers lawmaker appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘Cinema keeps that memory alive’: Suzannah Mirghani on Cotton Queen and Sudanese cinema
items.description: Sudanese-Russian filmmaker Suzannah Mirghani’s debut feature Cotton Queen (2025) follows Nafisa, a teenage girl growing up in a cotton-farming village where stories of Sudan’s colonial past collide with the pressures of modern development, tradition and changing agricultural practices. The film draws on Mirghani’s own memories of growing up in Sudan, while exploring the country’s relationship with cotton, the experiences of women and the impact of colonialism and war. The film was written, directed and produced by Mirghani, whose previous work includes the award-winning short film Al-Sit (2020). Cotton Queen premiered at Venice Film Festival Critics’ Week in 2025 after winning the 2022 ArteKino Award at L’Atelier de la Cinéfondation at the Cannes Film Festival. It has since received 10 awards at international festivals, including the Grand Prix for Fiction at the Geneva International Film Festival and Forum on Human Rights and Best Feature Film at the Rotterdam Arab Film Festival. Cotton Queen | Teaser Trailer. Suzannah Mirghani’s acclaimed Sudanese drama Cotton Queen arrives in cinemas across the UK and Ireland from 2 October. Mirghani spoke to Radio Dabanga about the personal memories behind Cotton Queen, the history embedded in Sudan’s cotton industry, the use of magical realism, and the challenges of recreating Sudan in Egypt after the outbreak of war. “Cotton connects so many themes.” Q&A with Suzannah Mirghani Radio Dabanga: What did this film mean to you personally, and why did you choose cotton as the central thread through which to explore those ideas? Suzannah Mirghani: The various vignettes in Cotton Queen are sourced from my memories of living in Sudan over a period of 10 years, from childhood to adolescence. I grew up in a hosh (garden) in Omdurman, where the women in my family, my grandmother, mother and sisters, were central figures in my life and where storytelling was an everyday activity. Director Suzannah Mirghani behind the scenes on the set of Cotton Queen (Photo: supplied) The film is influenced by the many mysteries and legends that extended across the neighbourhood as well as further afield in the Gezira region, where we would visit relatives, the river and the cotton fields. I often think back on my time in Sudan with great nostalgia. As an adult, however, as I began reading about the history of cotton in Sudan, grown in the very same places where I used to play, the romance unravelled. I began learning about the British colonial history of violence as well as the more recent introduction of genetically modified seeds, changing the face of the industry and the community’s relationship to the crop. The story of Cotton Queen connects important themes in Sudanese history and contemporary moments. Cotton has been both a blessing and curse, requiring tenderness and care from those who harvest it and attracting aggression and exploitation by those who seek to dominate it. I found cotton to be a perfect central subject for a story about Sudan. Cotton connects so many themes: the colonial history of Sudan, historical and contemporary industrial extraction and, most importantly, themes surrounding the community of women who have a very close relationship with cotton. They are the ones who harvest it, spin it, weave it and use it for their intimate bodily needs. The story of cotton binds all these themes together. When I was doing my research for the film, I came across the annual “Cotton Queen” beauty pageant, which was instituted initially in the 1930s in England, awarding a prize to the most beautiful girl working in the cotton industry during Sudan’s British colonial period. I knew immediately that Cotton Queen would be the title of my film. It is the nexus of patriarchy, colonialism and industry, and how all these forces are joined in the exploitation of women. In this film, I transform the concept of the Cotton Queen into one that is more reflective of a Sudanese girl awakening to her sense of self, beyond beauty and marriage, to have a real impact on her community. Radio Dabanga: You’ve spoken about wanting to keep the film as authentic as possible, and you can definitely feel that in the film. At the same time, the themes of magic and mysticism create an interesting interplay with that realism and the main character’s life experience. How did you approach those elements? Suzannah Mirghani: This film reflects two sides of my relationship to Sudan: one is as a child and the other is as an adult. I remember Sudan very fondly and have a great nostalgia for a country filled with fairytales, folklore, magic and mysticism. As an adult, however, I know this can be a naïve perspective that does not tell the full story of life in Sudan, which is also governed by a very harsh reality. In the film, Sudan is represented as a place where opposites exist simultaneously. It is both mythical and material; it is both beautiful and painful. The magical realist elements in my film are about imagining a new Sudan, a bittersweet dream, full of both nostalgia for something that never was, and hope for what can be. “Sudan is represented as a place where opposites exist simultaneously. It is both mythical and material; it is both beautiful and painful.” Radio Dabanga: The film is poignant. Even the moments that make you laugh are underpinned by something more serious. You also touch on issues including FGM and Sudan’s colonial history. Why was it important for you to explore these subjects through the film? Suzannah Mirghani: I did not set out to make a film about important issues. Many of these themes began to appear naturally as part of the story in the process of writing. I found that it was impossible to speak of cotton without remembering the British colonial history. I also found that in telling a coming-of-age story of a teenage girl, it was impossible not to explore issues related to the body, whether this was natural hormonal changes or bodily violence through tradition. There are so many hidden traumas in Sudan, both historical and contemporary, that are sublimated and normalised in everyday life. In the film, I try to capture some of these profound and mundane moments simultaneously. Radio Dabanga: You filmed the movie in Egypt rather than Sudan because of the war. What was it like working with actors and crew members who were living as refugees, and how did that experience shape the production? Suzannah Mirghani: Because of the war, many of the Sudanese cast and crew members were doubly displaced, first internally in Sudan, travelling from city to city seeking safety, and then externally, travelling to Egypt by any means. We waited patiently for the war to end so we could return to Sudan to resume lives and to continue work. Two years into the war, the conflict was still raging. We decided that it was time to take the film to the Sudanese cast and crew in Egypt, and to shoot the film there. Cast and crew gather on the set of Cotton Queen (Photo: supplied) We made sure to build the main sets, the houses and streets, by copying the architectural specifications of the original locations in Sudan. While all the Sudanese cast and crew members contributed advice or props to enhance the look and feel of the Sudanese set, the whole process was supervised by Simba Elmur, the costume designer who became the chief Sudanese cultural consultant. To give us the freedom to build, and to get away from the noise of Cairo, we built our main sets on open farmland on the outskirts of the city. Some of the sets were so real and so familiar, we often forgot that we were in Egypt. We really thought that we were in Sudan. Whenever we had a large group of Sudanese extras on set, they were in awe of the Sudanese village we created and relaxed in the space, chatting and singing, as though we were in Sudan. There was an extraordinary sense of community among the Sudanese on set. Of course, that meant that we were heartbroken to leave this imaginary Sudan every day after shooting. Building sets was easy. The most difficult part of the shoot was the emotional toll of the war. While the production of the film was affected by practical challenges as well as the emotional disappointment of not shooting in Sudan, by making this film together, we all felt that we could achieve something, that we could create something out of nothing, bringing both dignity and hope to those displaced. Even though we were all sad the film was not shot in our home country, recreating Sudan in Egypt gave the Sudanese cast and crew a sense of empowerment. We were able to do something positive for Sudan and honour the culture in a foreign country. “Building sets was easy. The most difficult part of the shoot was the emotional toll of the war.” Radio Dabanga: The film has received a lot of praise and awards. What does that recognition mean for you, and what do you think it says about the future of Sudanese film? Suzannah Mirghani : I am proud and honoured to have made this film with a Sudanese cast and crew who never gave up, and who managed to complete this film against so many odds: war, displacement, destruction of property, loss of livelihoods and the death of family members. For all of us, making this film was so much more than just making a film. It became a mission. It was a calling to create something for Sudan. As parts of the country were being destroyed, we were building. Sudanese cinema has always been about resilience and filmmakers produce their work regardless of the many restrictions and obstacles. The team behind Cotton Queen celebrates the film’s success at the Doha Film Festival (Photo: supplied) As Sudan is destroyed by war, there is a very real threat to the erasure of cultural memory. Cinema keeps that memory alive. From the audience side, we have seen a growing culture of appreciation. Screening Sudanese films has shown how interested Sudanese audiences are to see representation of themselves and the country on screen. Radio Dabanga: Given the state of Sudan now, four years into the war, what do you see as the practical steps needed to rebuild and strengthen the industry? And how can people support young and emerging artists? Suzannah Mirghani: Growing a film industry and sustaining an entire creative ecosystem has to be supported financially and institutionally for its long-term stability. These kinds of provisions and encouragements have always been lacking in Sudan, and especially in the current moment. With the war still ongoing and threatening the country’s stability, it’s difficult to sustain most sectors, let alone a creative industry. This situation, however, does not stop individual Sudanese filmmakers from continuing to work and to make their films in Sudan and elsewhere. The more individual Sudanese films continue to be produced, and the more they capture the public’s imagination, gaining awards and headlines, the more support future Sudanese filmmakers are likely to get from regional or international funding institutions. We all try to do our part in whatever small way we can. For instance, I run an online scriptwriting workshop called Aflam Banat, which helps Sudanese women shape their stories and prepare them for the next step of realising their work. I’ve seen the determination some of these writers have to produce their films, starting on a very small scale. I am encouraged to see many more young Sudanese filmmakers behind the camera. Director Suzannah Mirghani with lead actress Mihad Murtada (Photo: supplied) Many young up-and-coming filmmakers have an intense desire to tell their own stories. Mihad Murtada, the lead actress in Cotton Queen, has already started working on sets, film and commercials, to gain experience behind the scenes of a production. She’s also writing her own short scripts, which she hopes to develop and produce. There is so much creative potential. Young Sudanese filmmakers just need a degree of guidance, support and, of course, funding. Where to watch Cotton Queen Cotton Queen is receiving a UK and Ireland cinema release this October, with screenings supported by the BFI through funds from the National Lottery. UK and Ireland cinema release information and screening details are available through: Tape Collective . A poster for Cotton Queen ahead of its UK and Ireland screenings, which began on October 2. (Photo: TAPE Collective) Share article The post ‘Cinema keeps that memory alive’: Suzannah Mirghani on Cotton Queen and Sudanese cinema appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

items.title: Boxe : Le Bombardier Sou Toké Patrice remonte sur le ring le 31 octobre pour une dernière salve
items.description: 4 ceintures internationales, 85 combats, un surnom qui a fait trembler les rings : Sou Toké Patrice, dit « le Bombardier du Faso », mettra officiellement fin à sa carrière de boxeur professionnel le 31 octobre 2026. À l'occasion de son jubilé, il affrontera le Béninois Amoussou Anicet lors d'une soirée qui comprendra 5 combats amateurs en lever de rideau. Le même jour, il officialisera le lancement de « Faso Bolokourou », sa structure de promotion dédiée à la relance de la boxe professionnelle burkinabè. C'est une page qui se tourne, mais aussi une nouvelle qui s'ouvre. Sou Toké Patrice, figure emblématique de la boxe burkinabè, a annoncé la tenue de son jubilé pour le 31 octobre 2026. L'événement marquera la fin officielle de la carrière sportive de celui que tout le Faso connaît sous le nom du « Bombardier ». Sou Toké Patrice le Bombardier annonçant son jubilé et son agence pour la relance de la boxe burkinabè Le palmarès parle de lui-même. Double champion d'Afrique, en 2007 puis en 2013, Sou Toké a également conquis la ceinture WBC Méditerranéen le 14 février 2008 à la place de la Nation, à Ouagadougou, en battant le Franco-Algérien Yacine Chouaou par jet d'éponge au neuvième round. Le 18 décembre 2015, à la salle Antarès du Mans, il réalisait l'un des exploits les plus marquants de sa carrière. Le Bombardier avait bombardé le Français Nordine Arik après douze reprises et remporté les titres WBC Francophone et ABU des poids moyens. La Fédération française de boxe rapporte notamment que le Burkinabè avait envoyé son adversaire au tapis au quatrième round avant de s'imposer à la décision. Cette victoire à l'extérieur reste l'un des épisodes marquants de son parcours. Gagner une ceinture à l'extérieur relève de l'exploit dans le monde de la boxe professionnelle. Peu de boxeurs burkinabè peuvent se prévaloir d'un tel accomplissement. Sou Toké l'a fait. Il l'a fait avec la manière. Cette victoire lui avait permis de devenir le premier champion WBC Francophone des poids moyens. La conférence de presse pour annoncer le jubilé Débuté en 1994, le parcours du Bombardier l'a vu devenir champion novice six mois plus tard, puis champion du Burkina Faso l'année suivante, un titre qu'il conservera pendant sept ans. Au total, il aura livré 85 combats, remportant 30 victoires par KO et 49 aux points, pour seulement 6 défaites. Sa dernière apparition sur un ring remonte à 2016. Reconnu par ses pairs, Sou Toké a reçu le prix de l'Association des Journalistes Sportifs du Burkina en 2007, avant d'être fait Chevalier de l'ordre de mérite en 2008, puis Officier de l'ordre national en 2012 avec agrafe sport. Pour ce jubilé, le Bombardier montera une dernière fois sur le ring. Face à lui, le Béninois Anicet Amoussou. Ce nom n'est pas inconnu du public burkinabè : en octobre 2010, Amoussou, surnommé « Poison », avait affronté Boniface Kaboré dit « le Python » lors d'un gala international à la Maison du Peuple, s'inclinant aux points après un combat acharné. Faso Bolokourou, l'après-carrière du Bombardier Le jubilé ne sera pas seulement une célébration. Il marque aussi le point de départ d'un nouveau chapitre. Sou Toké Patrice a annoncé le lancement de « Faso Bolokourou », qui signifie « coup de poing au Faso » en dioula. Le promoteur justifie cette initiative par un constat lucide. Entre les années 2000 et 2015, la boxe professionnelle burkinabè a connu son âge d'or. Les galas à la place de la Nation, à la Maison du Peuple ou au Palais des Sports de Ouaga 2000 faisaient salle comble. Les titres internationaux s'accumulaient. Puis l'enthousiasme s'est étiolé, faute d'initiatives de promotion. « Faso Bolokourou » entend répondre à ce vide. Le Bombardier invitant le public burkinabè à sortir le 31 octobre pour sa dernière Après le jubilé, la structure prévoit d'organiser chaque mois des combats amateurs et chaque trimestre un combat professionnel, afin d'offrir aux jeunes boxeurs burkinabè des opportunités de se frotter à la concurrence internationale et de ramener des ceintures au pays. Le jubilé sera également l'occasion pour Sou Toké d'adresser ses remerciements au ministère des Sports, à la Fédération burkinabè de boxe, à son club de l'USFA, aux chefs traditionnels et à tous ses supporters. Un hommage sera rendu à l'ancien boxeur feu Nabaloum Dramane, dit « Boum Boum », décédé le 15 janvier 2026 à Ouagadougou . Figure emblématique de la boxe burkinabè, Boum Boum avait été trois fois champion d'Afrique et champion international WBC des poids plumes, marquant toute une génération par sa puissance de frappe. Lire aussi : Boxe : Sou Toké, le « Bombardier » demande la bénédiction du Moogho Naaba pour son jubilé Mathias KAM Minute.bf

items.title: FCT Police arrest suspect for raping, impregnating 12-year-old
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The FCT Police Command said on Saturday that its Anti-Kidnapping Unit, on 2nd October 2026, while on routine patrol around Airport Bridge Taxi Park, observed a fully tinted navy blue Volkswagen vehicle with registration number KMC567LQ parked with its windows wound up. Spokesperson of the command, SP Josephine Adeh, said the vehicle was observed to be shaking. “The officers, suspecting foul play, approached the vehicle and opened it, only to see one Zayyanu Halilu raping a twelve (12) year old minor. “Following the discovery, the suspect was promptly arrested and the victim was rescued. “Preliminary investigation revealed that the suspect had, on several occasions, lured and sexually abused the underaged victim in the said vehicle parked at the same location, with threats to “deal with her” if she reveals the abuse to anyone. “Medical examination also revealed that the victim is about three months pregnant as a result of the abuse. “The victim is currently receiving medical care and assessment, while the suspect remains in Police custody and will be charged to court upon conclusion of investigations. “The Commissioner of Police, FCT Command, CP Ahmed Muhammed Sanusi urges parents and guardians to remain vigilant and pay close attention to the whereabouts, safety and welfare of their wards at all times. “Members of the public are also enjoined to remain security conscious and promptly report suspicious activities or persons to the nearest police station or through the Command’s emergency lines: 08032003913, 08028940883.” The post FCT Police arrest suspect for raping, impregnating 12-year-old appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘Drone found NYSC abductors’ hideout, but camp is mined with IEDs’ — Imo CP
items.description: The Imo State Police Command has located the hideout where suspected kidnappers are holding abducted National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, members and other victims, Commissioner of Police Audu Garba Bosso has disclosed. Read Also: Bandits hijack two buses, kidnap corps members, others in Imo Bosso said security operatives used drones to track the abductors and were able to identify their exact location in the bush, but said the rescue operation had been delayed by intelligence indicating that the area was heavily mined with improvised explosive devices. Speaking to journalists on the ongoing operation, the Imo CP said security forces had already moved into the area and would continue efforts to safely reach the victims. “Yesterday we were in the bush; we trailed them up to a particular location. But at that point in time, we couldn’t move in to where the coordinates showed us where they are,” he said. According to him, the drones provided security operatives with the exact location of the abductors, but the presence of IEDs around the camp posed a major challenge to the operation. “But our predicament is that with the intel we have, the camp is mined with IEDs,” Bosso said. He added that security forces were preparing to deploy heavy equipment, including high-velocity vehicles, bulldozers and armoured personnel carriers, to gain access to the area and rescue the victims. “We are moving in there with high-velocity vehicles. We are moving with bulldozers and APCs to see how we are going to rescue these victims,” he said. The kidnap The victims were among passengers abducted after suspected gunmen attacked two buses along the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway in Imo State on October 1. The buses were reportedly carrying prospective corps members travelling from Ibadan to orientation camps in the South East and South South when they were attacked around the Umunoha axis of the road in Mbaitoli Local Government Area. The Imo State Police Command had earlier said 10 victims were rescued at the scene, while the exact number of those still in captivity was being verified. The Defence Headquarters subsequently said 20 passengers were abducted from the two buses, including several prospective corps members, while 10 passengers, among them eight identified prospective corps members, had been rescued. It said a joint search and rescue operation involving troops of Operation Udoka, the Nigeria Police Force and the Department of State Services, with support from the Nigerian Air Force, was ongoing to locate and rescue the remaining victims. items.title: AI Could Worsen a Common Cognitive Trap
items.description: One of humanity’s most remarkable cultural achievements is the division of explanatory labor. When my daughter came down with a fever, I solved the problem by consulting a pediatrician, who shared a likely diagnosis of the flu. Unlike the doctor, I wasn’t able to tell my daughter much about the mechanism by which the flu leads to fever, or exactly why it was so important for her to keep drinking fluids. But the explanation I acquired—roughly “fever because flu”—was what was needed to treat her. Society runs on this efficient type of information sharing. Just as coordinating specialized skills can streamline the fabrication of products—be it pins or cars or newspapers—coordinating specialized knowledge can facilitate the answering of questions. You can drive a car even if you don’t have the expertise to manufacture one yourself, and I benefited from the pediatrician’s explanation even though his understanding far exceeded my own. We can thank this divide-and-conquer method for many advancements in medicine and science, engineering and commerce; in fact, it has helped drive the accumulation of human knowledge across communities and over time. But it also leaves us susceptible to illusions of understanding: cases in which we mistake the understanding of others for our own. Humans’ sense of whom to ask for what is fine-tuned by evolution, culture, and personal experience. Even 3-to-5-year-olds are more likely to say that you should ask a doctor rather than a mechanic about fixing a broken arm, and a mechanic rather than a doctor about fixing a flat tire. As kids mature, they develop an even deeper understanding of expertise. In a 2004 study published in Child Development , for example, 11- and 12-year-olds tasked with finding out why tennis balls bounce better on the sidewalk than on grass were more likely to suggest asking someone who knows why bubble wrap keeps glass things from breaking (which is also relevant to physics) than someone who knows why tennis balls come in cans of three (which just happens to also involve tennis balls). Their choice of whom to ask was based on fundamental principles—not just superficial similarities. With plenty of time and care, years of education, and a healthy appetite for learning, most of us transition from children who know little about science or other expert domains to … adults who know little about science or other expert domains. Even those of us who acquire expertise in one area are unlikely to do so in many others. So the ability to track outside expertise is no less important for adults than it is for children. We need to know who can explain a child’s fever, a wilting plant, a clause in a will, or an imperfect soufflé—and research finds that adults seem to do this pretty well. (As a population, of course, we do not do this perfectly: Plenty of people trust in bad advice from their friends, influencers, and self-proclaimed experts.) A study from Germany found that even college students who aren’t science majors do a good job of guessing which kinds of scientific expertise are relevant to different scientific topics. So far, so good. The trouble arises when our connections to other minds become a little too seamless, and we start to lose track of where our own understanding ends and another’s begins. When we receive an explanation from an expert—such as “fever because flu”—we might mistakenly conclude that we’ve learned more than we really have. In fact, research finds that merely having access to expert answers can lead to illusions of understanding. In one set of studies, participants read about various fictional scientific discoveries and reported how well they understood the phenomenon described in each one. For instance, some participants received the following short passage: A May 19, 2014, study in the journal Geology reported the discovery of a new rock that scientists have thoroughly explained. The rock is similar to calcite, yet it glows in the absence of a light source. The authors of the study, Rittenour, Clark, and Xu, fully understand how it works; they provided a description of the remarkable appearance of the mineral and outlined future experiments. The passage didn’t actually include any explanations about why the rock glows. And yet, after reading the passage, participants thought they had some comprehension: what the authors call “a contagious sense of understanding,” because they seem to have caught it from the scientists described in the passage. When participants instead read that scientists “have not yet explained” the glowing rock, and that they “do not yet understand” how it works, there was no contagious sense of understanding; participant ratings of their own understanding nearly hit the bottom of the scale. More recent work has shown that a contagious sense of understanding can even infect our interactions with technology. In one study, participants learned about a bank’s “robo-adviser,” which could provide investment recommendations. Participants also learned that an explanation of how the robo-adviser works had been published in a scientific journal. But half were told that the explanation was available to them on the journal’s website, and half were told that the journal had a subscription paywall. Those who thought the explanation was available to them reported a better understanding of how the robo-adviser works. They also reported a greater likelihood of using the robo-adviser themselves. These results raise a pressing question. As information becomes more accessible through AI assistants, chatbots, and other technology, will these illusions of understanding become even more pronounced? Some early evidence suggests that the answer is yes. Several studies have now found that when people have information available to them through the internet, they overestimate how much they themselves know. For example, in one study, participants were asked to explain how something works, such as a zipper, and half were given access to the internet to “confirm the details of the explanation.” All participants were then asked how well they could offer detailed answers to unrelated questions, such as why cloudy nights are warm. Those who had access to the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves significantly more capable of explaining in the second part—suggesting that the experience of having more knowledge at their fingertips supported the illusion that the knowledge was in their own heads. Interactions with fast and informative chatbots will only heighten such illusions, but with a worrisome twist: The evidence so far suggests that humans aren’t great at tracking who knows what when it comes to large language models such as ChatGPT and Claude. For instance, when people in a study learned about an LLM that could correctly answer a question about economics, they expected it to correctly solve a basic algebra problem—but they were wrong. And when they learned that an LLM could answer a question about moral philosophy, they thought it could identify which character in a scenario had done something immoral—but they were wrong again. Participants almost certainly applied assumptions about how knowledge clusters in human minds to the AI system, and in both cases, this led them astray. The kinds of errors that AI systems make are likely to change as AI develops, and human intuition about AI will probably evolve alongside these changes. As we expand our community of explainers beyond human experts to chatbots and other forms of AI, we create new opportunities for human understanding. But we also introduce an increased potential for illusion and error. This article was adapted from Tania Lombrozo’s new book, Why We Ask Why: The Science of Explanation and the Human Drive to Understand .

items.title: Bait and Switch
items.description: Earlier this year, one of my fishing partners sent a 1 a.m. message to our group chat. It was a link to an Instagram post of an angler holding a sizable striped bass. Dappled gold and silver with a dozen distinct black lines that stretched from gills to tail, it would have been a gorgeous fish if not for two problems: Striped bass usually have seven stripes, not 12, and men usually have five fingers, not six. The photo, it seemed, was AI-generated. To say we were dismayed would be an understatement. From May to November each year, I spend most of my nights doing an extreme version of surf fishing for striped bass called “wetsuiting,” which involves wading or swimming out to distant ocean rocks and sandbars after dark. This kind of surf casting is a niche activity, and like many niche activities, the community for it is small. Wetsuiters can be found in a smattering of local fishing clubs throughout the Northeast—the typical range of the striped bass—but are primarily connected through Instagram, where some people, mostly for bragging rights, post images of fish they’ve caught. [ From the October 2024 issue: Inside the dangerous, secretive world of extreme fishing ] In our group chat, my fishing partners and I spend too much time scrutinizing photos of bass that other anglers have posted. People who fish are habitual liars (I say this fondly), and most of our conversations take the form of debates about whether a fish is really as big as someone claims. Lately, though, we’ve been asking a different question: Is that fish even real? In recent months, the small corner of Fishing Instagram devoted to surf casting has been plagued by a slow drip of AI-generated or AI-enhanced fish. Sometimes, the fraud is egregious—one of my friends, a fishing photographer, discovered that another angler had stolen one of his photos and crudely replaced my friend’s face with her own. More often, the distortions are subtle. Typically, a fish or fisherman looks ever so slightly off, usually in ways that a casual observer might not notice: A bass’s fins aren’t quite right, or the lure in its mouth looks oddly distorted, or the angler’s arms are a bit too long. In my favorite example, a man lifts a large striped bass just as he is getting pummeled by a wave. The scene looks daunting—until you realize that the ocean behind him is peaceful. Where did this rogue wave come from? One suspects that the enterprising angler, wanting to look more hard-core to his Instagram followers, prompted a bot to dial up the intensity. ChatGPT, make me look badass . Fishing magazines report growing concern about AI-generated fish in freelance photo submissions. I have written occasionally for the small online magazine Surfcaster’s Journal . Over the summer, the Journal announced that it would now run all manuscripts and photographs through AI-detection software. “For some reason, I naively assumed that fishermen wouldn’t stoop to the ‘core of the earth’ lows required to use AI to prop oneself up as a fisherman worthy of clicking the follow icon,” Dave Anderson, a well-respected wetsuiter and an editor at The Fisherman , wrote in an article lamenting the scourge of artificially generated fish on social media. “I was very wrong about this.” Angling, even extreme angling, is just a hobby, but although the stakes may be low, the anger about artificial fish is real. Partly, I think this is because of the work that being even remotely good at the sport demands. Striped bass move and feed in locally specific patterns that can take months or years to crack. There is a risk of drowning, and the mounting reports of bull sharks, tiger sharks , and great whites in the Northeast call attention to another layer of danger : We smell like fish, swim in dark water, and look like clumsy seals in our black neoprene. Wetsuiting does not change the world, but it is an activity that is hard and honest and, in that way, human. [ Read: The year great white sharks took over Maine ] Even taking a picture of a fish is demanding, requiring salt-water-proof cameras and often wading or swimming a bass back to shallow water, where it can safely be photographed and then released. The Photoshopping of fish pictures—and of the natural world in general—has been an issue for years, but AI, with its ability to conjure a simulacrum of reality out of nothing at all, is another matter. It automates away the need not only to photograph a fish, but to even catch one in the first place. The problem extends to other sports and hobbies, many of which are now defined by what Stuart Franklin—who took one of the celebrated “Tank Man” photos at Tiananmen Square—calls the “documentary impulse.” Social media has turbo-charged that impulse into an imperative. A good local skateboarder’s or surfer’s reputation would once have been built through word of mouth. Today, posted photographs and short-form videos may constitute the primary proof of ability. Concerns about AI slop are already being raised in cycling , skiing, and other activities . Climbing Magazine recently called out an AI-saturated YouTube channel purporting to chronicle climbing disasters that in fact never happened. As AI-generated fish have appeared more frequently in my social-media feed, I’ve been reminded of a scene in the bird-watching documentary Listers , where a highly competitive birder is asked whether he would keep bird-watching if the photo-logging website eBird disappeared. His answer—“No”—was unsettling, not least because one suspects that this sentiment is widespread in hobbies besides birding. I have often wondered if, for some of the wetsuiters who populate surf-casting Instagram, the dopamine hit from the likes and fire emoji is sweeter than the hit from catching the fish itself. Now that posted images are being looked upon with an ever greater degree of suspicion, I also wonder how much longer the dopamine hits will come for them at all. This is hardly the greatest challenge posed to humanity by the advent of AI. But hobbies, particularly those that require some measure of skill and endurance, have an influence that extends beyond those who directly participate in them. Free Solo , the Oscar-winning 2018 documentary about the death-defying rock climber Alex Honnold, found a wide audience outside the narrow world of climbing because people are invested in seeing other people do difficult things. I love videos of big-wave surfing even though I never plan to climb onto a surfboard. If AI makes it impossible to trust what we see, even something as simple as a surfing video, then we have lost more than the integrity of any one sport. We have lost the ability to believe in the accomplishments of others. This article appears in the November 2026 print edition with the headline “The Fish Are Getting Bigger .”

items.description: Pour la 68ᵉ celebration de l'independance de la Guinee, le president Mamadi Doumbouya a accorde, par decret, une grâce presidentielle, le 2 octobre, a 217 detenus, dont des prisonniers politiques a l'instar de Mamadou Aliou Bah, leader du Mouvement democratique liberal (MoDeL). L'opposant avait ete condamne a deux ans de prison ferme pour « offense et diffamation » a l'encontre du chef de l'etat, par le tribunal de premiere instance de Kaloum, le 7 janvier 2025, cette decision ayant ete confirmee en appel le 28 mai de la meme annee. Une grâce assortie d'un stage obligatoire d'encadrement civique et de preparation a la reinsertion Le decret presidentiel stipule aussi que la grâce est conditionnee a la participation a un stage obligatoire d'encadrement civique et de preparation a la reinsertion, d'une duree de 45 jours, destine a contribuer a la reinsertion sociale des beneficiaires et a leur sensibilisation aux valeurs civiques, citoyennes et republicaines. Un arrete conjoint qui sera emis ulterieurement par le ministre de la Justice et son homologue de la Defense nationale devra determiner les modalites d'organisation et de mise en œuvre de ce stage. Par cette mesure, les autorites guineennes disent vouloir concilier le retour progressif des detenus a la vie sociale tout en renforcant leur sensibilisation aux devoirs civiques et aux valeurs republicaines. Un arret de la Cour de justice de la CEDEAO avait ordonne la liberation du leader du MoDeL La grâce presidentielle dont beneficie Mamadou Aliou Bah survient a un moment ou la Cour de justice de la Communaute economique des etats de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (CEDEAO) a demande aux autorites judiciaires guineennes d'assurer le suivi de l'execution de son arret rendu le 25 juin dernier dans l'affaire opposant Aliou Bah a l'etat guineen. L'instance avait, en effet, ordonne la mise en liberte immediate et inconditionnelle du chef du parti d'opposition.

items.title: Ndume hails Tinubu over military salary increase
items.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja Former Senate Leader, Senator Ali Ndume, has commended President Bola Tinubu for fulfilling his pledge to increase the salaries of Armed Forces personnel. Ndume, who represents Borno South, gave the commendation in a statement made available to newsmen in Abuja on Saturday. Recall that the Presidency had in September announced its commitment to implement a new salary package for certain categories of military personnel. According to a statement signed by Presidential Media Aide, Bayo Onanuga, officers above the rank of colonel, including brigadier generals, major generals, lieutenant generals and generals, would get 30 percent increase. Those from colonel down to warrant officer 50 percent, while private to staff sergeant would get 80 percent. Onanuga said the package would raise the annual salary bill from N660 billion to N924 billion and benefit over 250,000 personnel. Director of Defence Information, Maj-Gen. Samaila Uba, confirmed implementation of the review to Defence Correspondents on Friday. Ndume, a former Chairman of the Senate Committee on Army, said the President has shown commitment to boosting morale. He said, “Making a pronouncement is one thing, redeeming your pledge is a different ball game entirely. “President Tinubu has shown times without number that he keeps to his words. It is heartwarming to note that the salary increment he promised the Nigerian Army has been redeemed.” The federal lawmaker further said, “I want to urge our officers to redouble their efforts to curtail insecurity since the present administration is doing everything to boost their morale. “They should do more now that they also have more troops on the ground with the recent recruitment. “The activation of the Army Aviation would also go a long way in complementing the efforts of the Air Force now that we also have attack helicopters in the six geo-political zones.” He restated his call for better synergy between infantry and Air Force in the war against insurgency and banditry. The post Ndume hails Tinubu over military salary increase appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Bassirou Diomaye Faye porte la voix de la Cedeao en Égypte
items.description: Le chef de l’État est à El-Alamein, en République arabe d’Égypte, en sa qualité de président en exercice de la Communauté économique des États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (Cedeao). Bassirou Diomaye Faye doit prendre part à la réunion de coordination mi-annuelle de l’Union africaine. Le président de la République a quitté Dakar hier pour El-Alamein, en République arabe d’Égypte, renseigne la Présidence de la République dans un communiqué publié sur sa page Facebook. Bassirou Diomaye Faye est en Égypte en sa qualité de président en exercice de la Cedeao, pour prendre part à la réunion de coordination mi-annuelle de l’Union africaine. « Le chef de l’État y retrouve ses pairs africains autour des priorités du développement et de l’intégration du continent. Ce séjour est tout autant consacré aux partenariats économiques du Sénégal. Le président de la République y rencontrera des décideurs et des investisseurs, à qui il présentera les opportunités qu’offre notre pays », précise la note de la Présidence. Après l’Égypte, le chef de l’État sera à Abuja, au Nigeria, pour une visite de travail au siège de la Commission de la Cedeao et l’installation des nouveaux juges de la Cour. Une tournée africaine qui va durer trois jours (2 au 4 octobre). Cette tournée africaine intervient quelques jours après la participation du chef de l’État à la 81e Assemblée générale des Nations unies à New York du 22 au 28 septembre 2026. Plus de 130 chefs d’État et de gouvernement ont pris part, à New York, à la semaine de haut niveau de la 81e session de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies. Pendant plusieurs jours, ils ont échangé sur le thème de cette année : « Établir la confiance, gérer la transformation : des Nations Unies au service de tous ». Lors de son séjour aux États-Unis, le chef de l’État s’est entretenu avec plusieurs responsables politiques et économiques. Il a eu une audience avec António Guterres, secrétaire général des Nations unies, Andrew Inglis, président directeur général (Pdg) de Kosmos Energy. Toujours en marge de la 81e session de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies, Bassirou Diomaye Faye a présidé la cérémonie de signature d’un protocole de partenariat entre la Société africaine de raffinage (Sar) et la compagnie turque Yamata en vue de la construction d’une deuxième raffinerie au Sénégal. Aliou Ngamby NDIAYE

items.title: Exploitation de chaîne de valeur riz en Casamance : 160 jeunes formés à Kabiline 2
items.description: La coopérative Kamano-Entente de Diouloulou et Déclic ont renforcé les compétences entrepreneuriales, managériales et financières de 160 jeunes des arrondissements de Kataba 1 et Sindian sur les enjeux de développement de leurs terroirs. BIGNONA – Au total 160 jeunes femmes, hommes et personnes en situation de handicap venus des arrondissements de Sindian et de Kataba 1 ont bénéficié d’une formation sur le leadership, l'entrepreneuriat, l'éducation financière et la contractualisation durant six mois à Kabiline 2. L'activité sous forme de bootcamp offerte par la coopérative Kamano-Entende de Diouloulou en partenariat avec Déclic et l’initiative Rizao (Riz en Afrique de l’Ouest) a renforcé la capacité des bénéficiaires sur les enjeux de développement de leurs terroirs. A lire aussi : Promotion des terroirs : l’Entente de Diouloulou et l’Asc de Badiana signent une convention « On a une grande satisfaction qui augure un lendemain meilleur pour les jeunes dans leurs différentes localités. On va créer de véritables champions entrepreneurs sur la chaîne de valeur riz », a déclaré vendredi Bassirou Coly, coordonnateur technique de l’Entente de Diouloulou, à la clôture du Bootcamp qui a démarré le 26 septembre. La formation entre dans le cadre du partenariat avec Rizao, dont le projet devrait créer à terme, en 2029, 16 mille emplois sur la chaîne de valeur riz. D’après Mohamed Samsidine Thiam, formateur, un des formateurs du bootcamp, il s’agissait d’incuber les jeunes aux opportunités qui gravitent autour de cette chaîne de valeur. Les bénéficiaires sont sortis de ce bootcamp conscients des opportunités à tirer de la filière riz. « J'ai acquis des connaissances qui vont m'aider dans l'entrepreneuriat », a dit Oulératou Badji bénéficiaire venant de Teloum, un village de la commune de Suelle dans l'arrondissement de Sindian. La demoiselle souhaite cependant un suivi par les formateurs. « Nous comptons poursuivre cet accompagnement à travers la mise en œuvre des activités pour faire des jeunes bénéficiaires de véritables entrepreneurs qui pourront développer la chaîne de valeur riz dans le département », a promis Alassane Aw, ingénieur agronome agent de Meda pour le compte de Rizao. Les jeunes ont aussi été formés sur leur développement personnel afin de leur permettre d'exploiter les potentialités économiques de leurs terroirs. « On peut avoir de futurs producteurs de riz et de fruits dans le département », espère le formateur Mohamed Samsidine Thiam. Kadidiatou SONKO (Correspondante)

items.title: Grâce présidentielle accordée à Aliou Bah : son mouvement, le MoDeL en prend acte et appelle au calme
items.description: Le Mouvement démocratique libéral (MoDeL) a réagi à la décision du président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, accordant une grâce présidentielle à son président, Mamadou Aliou Bah. Dans un communiqué publié à Conakry ce samedi 3 octobre 2026, la cellule de communication du parti dit prendre acte de cette décision, qui intervient après près de 22 mois de détention. Cette mesure ouvre désormais la voie à la libération de Mamadou Aliou Bah et à son retour auprès de sa famille, de ses proches et de ses concitoyens. Le MoDeL accueille cette décision « avec sérénité et lucidité » et appelle ses militants, ses sympathisants ainsi que l’ensemble des citoyens à faire preuve de retenue et de responsabilité. Le parti précise par ailleurs qu’il tiendra régulièrement l’opinion publique informée de l’évolution du processus de libération de son président.

items.title: IEA members release 325m barrels of oil from strategic reserves
items.description: The International Energy Agency said Saturday that member countries had so far released 325 million barrels of oil and oil-derivative products from strategic reserves, from 400 million barrels promised in March. The update came a day after G7 countries, in coordination with the IEA, agreed to immediately release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil to ease global energy supply concerns caused by fallout from the US-Iran war. The G7 did not say whether the 100 million barrels included the outstanding 75 million barrels from the March IEA commitment, or came on top of that. The US government of President Donald Trump has been pressuring allies to release diesel reserves to ease a spike in prices for the fuel, being felt in America and elsewhere. Restricted diesel supplies is one of the consequences of the war in the Middle East, where Iran has been throttling ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for US and Israeli attacks. Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, part of the fightback against Moscow’s strikes, have also affected the market. The IEA said in a statement on Saturday that “around 325 million barrels of the IEA collective action announced on 11 March have so far been released, representing over 80 percent of the 400 million barrels originally pledged in the action”. The March pledge was offered up by the IEA’s 32 member countries, a grouping that includes all the G7 nations: of Britain, Canada, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States. The G7 countries on Friday agreed to release over the next four months 100 million barrels of oil and oil-derivative products, “including a frontloaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days”. They also said there would be no ban on diesel exports between them — heading off a threat Washington had brandished, and which Trump later said would not be enacted. items.title: ‘We are waiting for the delegates’ – NPP explains delay in voting at Kumasi conference
items.description: The Acting National Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Danquah Smith Buttey, has attributed the delay in the commencement of voting at the party’s National Delegates Conference in Kumasi to the late arrival of delegates. Speaking at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium on Saturday, October 3, Mr Buttey said voting would begin once the required number of delegates had arrived at the venue. “We are waiting for the delegates. They are not here. So, if 1/3 of them comes then we start.” When asked what was causing the delay, the Acting National Chairman said he could not give a specific reason, noting that the delegates were still at their various locations. “I don’t know. They are there at their various places.” Mr Buttey was also asked about allegations that some candidates were still engaging delegates on the day of the election, potentially contributing to the delay. He dismissed the suggestion as unusual, saying such engagements had been a feature of the party’s internal elections. “It has always been so. This is not new.” The NPP’s National Delegates Conference and national officers’ elections are being held at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi, with 7,163 delegates expected to participate in the exercise. The conference includes the consideration of proposed constitutional amendments, followed by the election of the party’s national officers.

items.title: Formation du gouvernement : des membres du PAM s’opposent à une alliance avec le RNI
items.description: Lors de la session extraordinaire du Conseil national du Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM), tenue ce samedi à Skhirat, des voix se sont élevées contre la participation du Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI) au prochain gouvernement qui sera dirigé par Fatima Zahra Mansouri, tandis que d’autres ont appelé à laisser une plus grande marge de manœuvre à la commission chargée des consultations gouvernementales. Hicham El Mhajri, membre du bureau politique du PAM, a exprimé, lors de son intervention à huis clos, son opposition à une alliance avec le RNI, appelant les membres du Conseil national à soutenir sa position. El Mhajri a indiqué avoir clairement exprimé son point de vue, estimant que les résultats des élections avaient envoyé des messages politiques qui devraient être pris en compte lors de la définition de la nature de la prochaine coalition gouvernementale. La position d’El Mhajri a suscité des réactions dans la salle, plusieurs membres du Conseil national ayant applaudi, ce qui témoigne de l’existence, au sein du Conseil, d’une tendance favorable à l’exclusion du RNI de la future coalition gouvernementale. L’ancienne parlementaire Nadia Bouzandoufa a défendu une position similaire, estimant qu’une alliance avec le RNI serait « contraire à la justesse », et insistant sur la nécessité de respecter les messages exprimés par les urnes. D’autres intervenants au sein du Conseil national ont également défendu cette position, considérant que la situation exigeait de donner une traduction politique claire aux résultats des élections et de ne pas reconduire des alliances dont, selon les partisans de cette orientation, les électeurs auraient exprimé le rejet. À l’inverse, El Khatat Yenja, membre du bureau politique du parti, a appelé à ne pas exclure à l’avance quelque partie que ce soit, soulignant la nécessité de laisser à la commission chargée des consultations toute latitude pour mener les négociations avec les autres formations politiques. Yenja a insisté sur le fait que l’imposition de restrictions préalables au processus de consultations pourrait compliquer les négociations. Il a appelé à faire confiance à la commission chargée de gérer cette étape, ainsi qu’aux informations dont elle dispose concernant les contraintes liées à la formation du gouvernement. Le début de la séance a également été marqué par un débat entre plusieurs membres du Conseil national sur les limites de l’intervention des membres du bureau politique dans l’orientation des discussions. Fatima Zahra Mansouri est alors intervenue pour rappeler que la session était consacrée à l’examen des alliances gouvernementales et que les membres du bureau politique, en leur qualité de membres du Conseil national, avaient le droit d’exprimer leurs opinions. D’autres voix au sein du Conseil ont par ailleurs appelé à accorder à Mansouri, en sa qualité de cheffe du gouvernement désignée, une marge de manœuvre plus large dans la conduite des consultations, afin qu’elle puisse diriger les négociations dans l’intérêt du pays et du parti. The post Formation du gouvernement : des membres du PAM s’opposent à une alliance avec le RNI appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Sonede | Coupures d’eau potable à partir du mardi 6 octobre au nord de Tunis
items.description: On peut difficilement imaginer que la Société nationale d’exploitation et de distribution des eaux (Sonede) puisse multiplier les coupures d’eau potable, de manière intermittente mais régulière, dans pratiquement toutes les régions du pays, pour alimenter la colère des citoyens et les remonter contre le pouvoir en place, comme le laissent entendre de temps en temps certains hauts responsables sans apporter la moindre preuve tangible d’un tel… «complot». Les responsables de la Sonede, en tout cas, restent imperturbables et poursuivent leur bonhomme de chemin, sans ressentir le besoin de répondre à de telles accusations, à leurs yeux fantaisistes ô combien ! D’ailleurs, ils viennent de publier, ce samedi 3 octobre 2026, un énième communiqué annonçant des perturbations et des coupures dans le réseau de distribution de l’eau potable dans plusieurs villes et quartiers de la banlieue nord de Tunis. Ces perturbations et coupures seraient enregistrées pendant 36 heures, à partir du mardi 6 octobre à 01h00 du matin, dans les zones suivantes, précise-t-on : Délégation de La Marsa : quartiers Bouselsla, Borj El Houki, Ettabek, El Houkkam, Sidi Daoud et Bhar Lazrag. Délégation de La Goulette (secteur Le Kram) : Hadaeq Carthage et Ain Zaghouan Nord et Sud. Délégation de Carthage : quartier Mohamed Ali et Carthage Byrsa. Délégation de Cité El Khadra : Les Berges du Lac 1. Délégation de La Goulette : Les Berges du Lac 2, quartiers Taieb Mehiri, El Wahat, Essalama et El Aouina. Délégation de Soukra : Dar Fadhal. Le rétablissement progressif de l’approvisionnement en eau est prévu à partir de 13h00 le mercredi 7 octobre, précise le même communiqué, ajoutant que cette intervention s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’achèvement des travaux du projet de protection de la zone de La Marsa contre les inondations et de la couverture du canal d’écoulement de l’Oued Ettabek, au niveau de la rue Ibn Rachiq (quartier Bhar Lazrag). «Il s’est avéré qu’une conduite de distribution principale, d’un diamètre de 1000 mm, entravait le tracé des travaux et empêchait leur poursuite dans les délais prévus, rendant son déplacement impératif» , précise encore la Sonede, ajoutant qu’après coordination avec les différents services concernés, ses équipes ont programmé les travaux de déplacement et de raccordement de ladite conduite, à partir du mardi 6 octobre à 01h00 du matin. «Les travaux se poursuivraient sans interruption, jour et nuit, pendant toute la durée de l’intervention et les équipes techniques seront mobilisées sur le terrain et mettront tout en œuvre pour achever les travaux dans les meilleurs délais, afin de rétablir l’approvisionnement normal en eau» , assure-t-on, en invitant «les citoyens et les établissements à prendre les précautions nécessaires et à constituer des réserves d’eau pour couvrir leurs besoins essentiels durant cette période.» Par ailleurs, la Sonede a annoncé «la mise à disposition de cinq camions-citernes (d’une capacité de 10 m³ chacun) pour approvisionner en eau potable, en cas de besoin, les établissements sensibles tels que les écoles, les lycées et les structures de santé.» I. items.title: Floriculture : dans l’oasis des pépiniéristes de Pikine-Technopole
items.description: Sous un soleil de plomb à Pikine-Technopole, l'agitation du trafic fait face au calme d'une oasis de verdure. Installés le long des grands axes, des pépiniéristes perpétuent un savoir-faire précieux. Malgré la salinité des sols et les revenus incertains, ces artisans transforment la contrainte urbaine en vitrine végétale pour la capitale. Une oasis de verdure attire le regard des automobilistes et des passants : nous ne sommes pas dans la forêt amazonienne, mais bien à Pikine-Technopole. C'est ici que s’installent les artisans fleuristes qui ont fait de cet espace leur univers. En ce mercredi 29 septembre, le soleil de plomb oblige les fleuristes à trouver refuge au cœur de leurs jardins. Malgré la chaleur suffocante, les vendeurs s’activent pour prendre soin de leurs plantes. Parmi eux, Mame Gor Ndiaye opère dans son espace dénommé ”Touba Jardin“. Installé sur ce site depuis 2018, pour perpétuer le legs de son père, il observe quotidiennement le va-et-vient des clients, venus de tous les milieux sociaux et de toutes tranches d’âge. « Tout le monde vient ici : des hommes, des femmes, des enfants. Nous accueillons vraiment toute la population », explique-t-il chaleureusement. A lire aussi : Dakar à l’heure des JOJ : au cœur du marché Sandaga, le commerce affûte ses armes Sur le plan économique, la vente de fleurs connaît des fluctuations au fil de l'année. Si l'affluence varie d'un jour à l'autre, la présence d'une clientèle fidèle et d'acheteurs réguliers permet aux artisans d'assurer leurs besoins quotidiens. « Je ne peux pas donner de chiffre exact par jour, mais il suffit parfois d'un seul grand achat pour nous faire tenir plusieurs jours », confie Mame Gor. Les périodes de forte affluence coïncident souvent avec les grandes fêtes : « C’est surtout durant les événements comme la Tabaski ou les fêtes de fin d’année que la demande explose. » L'artisan entrevoit également de belles opportunités avec les grands rendez-vous à venir : « Pour les Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse, j'espère que cela aura un impact positif. Je travaille habituellement avec des décorateurs événementiels lors des grandes cérémonies. En ce moment, je prépare des échantillons pour un partenariat avec Khelcom Bâches. Ce n'est que le début, mais c'est très prometteur. » Entre embellissement urbain et mission sociale Au-delà du commerce, Mame Gor Ndiaye souligne la portée sociale et environnementale de son métier le long des voies rapides : « L'environnement y gagne en premier, les passants en second, et l'État en troisième. Aménager un endroit permet de réduire l'insécurité et d'assainir l'espace. Sans ces aménagements, ce serait l'anarchie. Ici, les usagers profitent d'un cadre propre et présentable, loin des décharges sauvages. C'est un bénéfice partagé. » Il rappelle d'ailleurs un engagement réciproque : « Après le déguerpissement des fleuristes de la Patte d'Oie, les autorités nous ont accordé cet espace à condition que nous entretenions et décorions les abords de la route. » Le défi permanent de la salinité des sols Cependant, le quotidien de l'horticulteur est contraint par une menace naturelle : la salinité des sols. « Il y a des zones où la terre est tellement salée que je n'ai pas pu y travailler cette saison. Même pour la culture hors-sol, le sel contenu dans la terre pose problème. » Pour y remédier, Mame Gor a développé sa propre méthode : « La solution réside dans l'utilisation d'engrais biologique et de terreau. Cela exige des moyens financiers importants, car il faut apporter de grandes quantités et arroser abondamment pour diluer la concentration saline. » Un peu plus loin sur le site, Ibou Tine, la quarantaine passée, partage la même passion. Installé ici depuis trois ans, il exerce le métier depuis 2004. « À mes débuts, je me déplaçais en ville pour faire de l'entretien de jardins », se rappelle-t-il. L’air décontracté, discutant avec ses collègues assis à même le sol, il confirme la réalité économique du secteur : « L'activité est imprévisible : un client peut acheter une seule potée tandis qu'un autre repartira avec des dizaines de plants. Mais l'essentiel est là : notre travail nous permet de subvenir à nos besoins. » Ingéniosité et système D au quotidien Au cœur de cette bande verdoyante, l'ingéniosité pallie souvent le manque de moyens. Dans sa pépinière, Bathie Sène s'active, couteau en main, à découper des bidons en plastique de 10 litres pour confectionner des pots de fortune destinés à ses jeunes pousses. Tout en façonnant ces supports de culture, le pépiniériste détaille la diversité de son catalogue : « Nous proposons plusieurs variétés : oreilles d’éléphant, crotons, vétivers, sapins, palmiers… » Face au fléau de la salinisation, Bathie adopte lui aussi des méthodes naturelles : « Nous utilisons du fumier, notamment du fumier de fosse, pour atténuer l'impact du sel sur les racines. » Par leur savoir-faire et leur persévérance, ces artisans de l’environnement ne font pas que vendre des plantes : ils façonnent un paysage urbain plus respirable, transformant la contrainte minérale des axes routiers en une vitrine végétale vivante. Fatou NGOM (Stagiaire)

items.title: Exposition gouvernementale Le ministre chargé de la guerre, Célestin Simporé échange avec les citoyens
items.description: Le ministre d’Etat, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, le général de division, Célestin Simporé, a animé la première séance du « Dialogue avec le Peuple » placée sur le thème « Gouvernance, Sécurité nationale : le peuple debout vous rend compte », vendredi 2 octobre 2026, au SIAO. Le ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, le général de division, Célestin Simporé s’est prêté à un exercice de redevabilité du gouvernement envers le peuple vendredi 2 octobre 2026 au SIAO. En effet le grand oral initié dans le cadre de la 2e phase de la IIIe édition des Journées nationales d’engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne (JEPPC) qui se tient du 2 au 9 octobre 2026 a permis au chef du département de faire le point des actions majeures menées pour la reconquête du territoire national. Il a confié que dès octobre 2022 pour renforcer les capacités opérationnelles de l’armée 90 000 Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie communaux et nationaux ont été enrôlés. L'organisation des Forces d'armées nationale (FAN) a connu de profondes mutations car de trois régions militaires, elles sont passées à six. Pour un meilleur maillage sécuritaire les premiers Bataillons d'intervention rapide (BIR) ont été créés en novembre 2022, a indiqué le ministre d’Etat. « De six BIR au départ, en espace d’un an, nous sommes à une trentaine déployée sur l'ensemble du territoire », a-t-il poursuivi. La décision d'associer les forces de sécurité intérieure à la défense du territoire a permis aux corps paramilitaires de s'impliquer dans la guerre contre le terrorisme. Pour lui, la reconquête des zones autrefois interdites aux populations civiles est bien en marche. « Aucune partie du territoire ne nous échappe » Il s’est rappelle des reprises de la ville de Solenzo, des vallées du Sourou et de Di, la défense de la ville de Djibo, la sécurisation des localités de Diapaga, Titao, Solhan, Sebba… « Aujourd'hui, il n'existe pas un seul mètre carré du territoire national où nos forces combattantes ne peuvent y mettre les pieds. Les populations rejoignent les villages autrefois occupés et mènent leurs activités économiques. Le retour de l'administration se fait tous les jours et les services sociaux de base sont fonctionnels », a rassuré le général de division Célestin Simporé. Il a notifié que depuis 2022, les effectifs des recrutements ont été multipliés pour garantir une défense souveraine du territoire. Des avancements à titre exceptionnel ont été également adoptés pour encourager les éléments sur le terrain. Il s’agit notamment, de la distinction honorifique, de la croix du combattant, désormais décerner pour récompenser la bravoure des combattants au front. Pour ce qui est des équipements il a affirmé que les unités sont aujourd’hui équipées en armements individuels, collectifs et de façon conséquente, avec tous les moyens de protection. « Des dispositions ont été prises pour que la création en juillet 2023 de l’Agence de soutien aux veuves, orphelins et victimes de guerre pour coordonner l'aide aux familles de combattants et victimes de l’insécurité », a-t-il renseigné. Le ministre a souligné que 100000 réservistes sont en cours de recrutement vise à donner la possibilité à tous les citoyens de participer à la défense du pays. Il a, par ailleurs, évoqué des avancées enregistrées dans le cadre la Confédération des Etats du Sahel AES). « A ce jour la force unifiée est mise en place et continue sa montée en puissance pour son opérationnalisation. L'espace AES deviendra un sanctuaire pour le terrorisme », a-t-il prévenu. L’activité consacrée à l’exposition gouvernementale a également permis à des citoyens venus notamment de Mangodara dans le Kénédougou, Bourzanga dans les Koulsé, Dano dans le Yoba, etc., d’échanger avec le ministre sur leurs préoccupations. Elles ont porté essentiellement sur les difficultés d’accès à certaines localités, la sécurisation des frontières, la mobilisation des VDP, le recrutement des 100000 réservistes, la lutte contre le grand banditisme. Le ministre chargé de la guerre a apporté des éclairages précis sur les dispositifs sécuritaires déployés pour consolider la protection des personnes et des biens. Sur le grand banditisme, le ministre de la défense a signalé que des stratégies sont en cours pour faire à cette forme de criminalité. Pour les enregistrements des réservistes il a annoncé que des dispositifs vont être déployés dans les régions pour faciliter le travail. Le ministre a, par ailleurs, invité les jeunes à s’impliquer davantage dans les actions du gouvernement car il s'agit de leur garantir un avenir meilleur. ‎Aly SAWADOGO

items.title: Top 10 richest women in the world
items.description: The world’s richest women have built and inherited fortunes spanning retail, beauty, shipping, finance, mining, technology and philanthropy, with several of them tied to some of the biggest family-owned businesses in the world. According to Forbes’ Real-Time Billionaires list as of October 3, 2026, Alice Walton is the world’s richest woman, with an estimated net worth of $115.7 billion. She is followed by L’Oréal heiress Françoise Bettencourt Meyers and her family, with $90.4 billion, while Julia Koch and her family rank third with $84.6 billion. Here are the 10 richest women on Forbes’ real-time list as of October 3, 2026. 1. Alice Walton — $115.7 billion At 76, Alice Walton is the only daughter of Walmart founder Sam Walton and the richest woman in the world, according to Forbes’ real-time ranking. Her fortune, estimated at $115.7 billion, comes from Walmart, but unlike her brothers Rob and Jim, she chose not to serve on the company’s board. Instead, she has focused much of her attention on art and philanthropy. Walton’s most prominent cultural project is the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, which she opened in 2011 in Bentonville, Arkansas, the hometown of the Walton family. The museum houses works by artists including Andy Warhol, Norman Rockwell and Mark Rothko, reflecting Walton’s long-standing interest in art and philanthropy. 2. Françoise Bettencourt Meyers & family — $90.4 billion Françoise Bettencourt Meyers, 73, is the granddaughter of L’Oréal founder Eugène Schueller and the heir to one of the world’s largest beauty fortunes. She and her immediate family own more than a third of the publicly traded cosmetics giant, giving the family an estimated fortune of $90.4 billion. Bettencourt Meyers served on L’Oréal’s board from 1997 until 2025, when her son Jean-Victor Meyers succeeded her as vice chairman. Her other son, Nicolas Meyers, is also a director. She became the family’s principal L’Oréal heiress in 2017 following the death of her mother, Liliane Bettencourt, at 94. 3. Julia Koch & family — $84.6 billion Julia Koch and her three children inherited a 42 per cent stake in Koch, Inc., formerly known as Koch Industries, following the death of her husband, David Koch, in 2019. Forbes estimates the family’s fortune at $84.6 billion, making Koch, 64, the third-richest woman on the real-time list. An Iowa native, Koch moved to New York City in the 1980s and worked as an assistant to fashion designer Adolfo. During that period, she worked with several high-profile clients, including former US First Lady Nancy Reagan. Her wealth is now primarily tied to her family’s stake in Koch, Inc. 4. Jacqueline Mars — $50.3 billion Jacqueline Mars, 86, owns an estimated one-third of Mars, the privately held candy, food and pet-care company founded by her grandfather. Her fortune stands at $50.3 billion, placing her among the world’s wealthiest women. Mars worked for the family company for nearly two decades and remained on its board until 2016. Her wealth is tied to the vast business interests of Mars, which has grown far beyond the confectionery products associated with its name to include food and pet-care businesses. 5. Iris Fontbona & family — $47.4 billion Iris Fontbona, 83, inherited her fortune after the death of her husband, Chilean businessman Andrónico Luksic, in 2005. Luksic had built a business empire spanning mining and beverages before his death from cancer. He left his businesses to Fontbona and their three sons. Fontbona and her children control Antofagasta Plc, a London-listed company that owns copper mines in Chile. The family’s fortune is estimated at $47.4 billion, with mining serving as its principal source of wealth. Fontbona’s son Guillermo Luksic died of lung cancer in 2013 at the age of 57. 6. Rafaela Aponte-Diamant — $46.1 billion Rafaela Aponte-Diamant, 81, stands out on the list as a self-made billionaire who built her fortune in the shipping industry alongside her husband, Gianluigi. The couple each own a 50 per cent stake in MSC, described by Forbes as the world’s largest shipping line. Her real-time net worth is estimated at $46.1 billion. The couple’s business journey began after they met on the Italian island of Capri in the 1960s, when Gianluigi was a ship captain. In 1970, they entered the shipping business together by purchasing a ship with a $200,000 loan, eventually building the global shipping company that forms the foundation of their fortune. 7. Abigail Johnson — $41.6 billion Abigail Johnson, 64, is chairman and CEO of Fidelity Investments, the financial services giant founded by her grandfather, Edward C. Johnson II, in Boston in 1946. She became CEO in 2014, succeeding her father, and has served as chairman since 2016. Forbes estimates her fortune at $41.6 billion. Johnson owns an estimated 29 per cent of Fidelity. As of December 2025, the company managed $7.1 trillion in discretionary assets, making the family’s long-standing financial-services business the primary source of her wealth. 8. Savitri Jindal & family — $38.4 billion Savitri Jindal, 76, chairs the O.P. Jindal Group, whose businesses span steel, power, cement and infrastructure. Her estimated fortune of $38.4 billion is largely tied to the industrial empire founded by her late husband, Om Prakash Jindal. After O.P. Jindal died in a helicopter crash in 2005, his business interests were divided among his four sons, who now operate the companies independently. Some of the group’s biggest assets are overseen by her Mumbai-based son Sajjan Jindal, who runs businesses including JSW Steel, JSW Cement and JSW Paints. 9. Marilyn Simons & family — $36.6 billion Marilyn Simons, 75, inherited her fortune from her late husband, Jim Simons, the mathematician and founder of quantitative hedge fund Renaissance Technologies. Jim Simons died in 2024 at the age of 86. Forbes puts Marilyn Simons and her family’s fortune at $36.6 billion. Simons holds a PhD in economics from Stony Brook University, where she met her husband. She now chairs the Simons Foundation, which has $4.5 billion in assets and is the primary funder of Math for America, extending the family’s influence beyond finance into education and research. 10. Melinda French Gates — $34.5 billion Melinda French Gates, 62, is the founder of Pivotal Philanthropies Foundation and one of the most prominent women in global philanthropy. Forbes estimates her real-time net worth at $34.5 billion, with Microsoft listed as her source of wealth. In 2024, French Gates resigned as co-chair of the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation after nearly 24 years with the organisation. Her departure came three years after her divorce from Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates in 2021, with Forbes estimating that she received a $25 billion settlement from the divorce. The post Top 10 richest women in the world appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Six individus arrêtés pour association de malfaiteurs et apologie d’actes contre nature
items.description: Le Commissariat d’arrondissement de la Médina (au Sénégal ) a procédé, le 30 septembre 2026, à la conduite au parquet de six individus pour association de malfaiteurs, apologie d’actes contre nature et transmission volontaire du VIH. Dans la nuit du 25 au 26 septembre 2026, à la suite d’un attroupement survenu à l’angle de la Rue 25 et de la Rue 04 à la Médina, les éléments du service sont intervenus pour rétablir l’ordre public. Menacés de violences par un groupe d'individus présents sur les lieux, six (06) personnes ont été extirpées et acheminées au poste pour leur propre sécurité. Toutefois, à l'issue des premières constatations, ces derniers ont été placés en garde à vue pour des faits d’actes contre nature portés à leur encontre. L'approfondissement des investigations a permis de mettre en lumière les éléments suivants : • L’un des mis en cause a déclaré avoir entretenu, au cours du mois de septembre 2026, une relation sexuelle avec un individu de sexe masculin — rencontré via le réseau social TikTok — en contrepartie de la somme de 12 000 FCFA. • L’un des mis en cause a par ailleurs admis avoir été victime, par le passé, de plusieurs agressions sexuelles de la part d'individus de sexe masculin. • Les dépistages sérologiques du VIH pratiqués sur les mis en cause, dont les résultats ont été transmis par le médecin-traitant, se sont révélés positifs pour plusieurs d’entre eux. Une exploitation technique approfondie a été menée par la Division Spéciale de Lutte contre la Cybercriminalité (DSLC) sur les quatre (04) téléphones portables saisis dans le cadre de cette procédure. L’analyse des échanges WhatsApp (photographies, vidéos et messages à caractère sexuel) de cette bande, dénommée « Sabar Monument », a permis d'établir des relations et des attirances sexuelles avérées entre les membres. Les mis en cause ont été déférés au parquet pour répondre de leurs actes. La Police est et reste mobilisée et appelle ainsi la population à contacter le 800 00 17 00 pour toute information utile. Police nationale du Sénégal L’article Six individus arrêtés pour association de malfaiteurs et apologie d’actes contre nature est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .
